item.title: 【夜读】人生，要懂得转弯
item.description:
1


思维转个弯，发现意想不到的路


你有没有这样的时刻：明明很努力了，却还是等不到想要的结果；明明觉得没有做错什么，却好像总是常常碰壁。其实，你需要的或许不是更多的勇气，而是一个转弯。


你看小溪遇到山石阻挡，不会停下来哭泣，它懂得绕过去，继续奔向大海；大雁南飞遇到逆风，不会硬顶着气流，它懂得变换队形、调整方向，找到更省力的航线。


很多时候，困住我们的不是眼前的绝境，而是脑子里的“死胡同”。向前一步是墙，退后一步是崖，我们便以为无路可走，却忘了路的旁边还有路。


阳光转个弯，能照进直射不到的角落；思维转个弯，就能看见原本看不见的出口。那些“山重水复疑无路”的时刻，往往只差一个转身，便是“柳暗花明又一村”。


2


心态转个弯，欣赏不一样的风景


人生就像一列行进的列车。有人懂得该行时行、该停时停，走走停停，一路风光尽收眼底；有人只顾埋头赶路，一味疾驰，等到发现方向不对，早已错过了沿途的风景。


路在脚下，更在心里，心随路转，路便常宽。遇到好事，顺其自然，尽力而为；碰上难处，不钻牛角尖，心才舒坦。


没有谁的生活是完美的，但我们可以用积极的心态去面对一切。遇到烦恼时，不妨让心态转个弯——纠结怨愤往往是徒劳无功的，焦虑烦躁只会把我们困在原地，换种心态、换个角度，你会发现，一切远没有想象中那么糟糕。


凡事都有两个面。那些让我们焦头烂额的坎，或许正藏着转机；那条看似绕了远的路，也许正通向更好的风景。换个心态去看，生活便多一分顺心与愉悦。


3


人生转个弯，学着与生活和解


人生这条路，从来不是只有直行一个选项。当你拼尽全力，依然事与愿违时，别再在原地苦苦挣扎。与其对着一扇紧闭的门黯然神伤，不如转身看看，旁边的那扇窗是否已经为你打开。


那些迟迟没有回复的消息，就别再发了；那段让你委曲求全的关系，就果断放手。真正的成熟，是懂得在适当的时候，给自己一个重新开始的机会。


想不通时，换个念头；看不开时，换个角度；走不通时，就绕个弯。学着与自己的生活和解，当你不再和自己较劲，或许就能另辟蹊径，路也将越走越宽。


未来，愿你在该坚持时坚定不移，在该转弯时洒脱从容。要相信，转弯之后的风景，或许更值得期待。


来源：人民日报夜读综合 |  主播：赵文龙

item.title: Trump's opponents are planning how to reverse his changes to the presidency
item.description:
Democratic House members are writing bills to rein in a president’s emergency powers. Lawyers are strategizing about how to insulate the Justice Department from presidential influence. A House measure would block a president from unilaterally remodeling the White House. Ethicists are writing rules to prevent a future first family from self-dealing.

Throughout Washington and beyond, President Donald Trump’s opponents are scrambling to ensure that after he leaves office, the changes he has imposed on the presidency, and the country, will fade with him.

Subscribe to The Post Most newsletter for the most important and interesting stories from The Washington Post.

Whether they succeed could determine whether Trump’s aggressive exercise of executive powers will be limited to a finite stretch of U.S. history or will instead become a model for every president to come.

Rep. Jamie Raskin (Maryland), the top Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, said that Trump’s uses of presidential power can and must be reversed - but doing so will take decades.

“We have a massive reconstruction task ahead of us,” Raskin said in an interview. “Fortunately, reconstruction has a great history in our country, and when it’s allowed to work, it has been a lot more successful than either authoritarianism or revolution. … We will have to go department by department, subject by subject, and public purpose by public purpose to determine what we salvage and what we re-create.”

From the beginning of the republic, the three branches have jostled for control over spending, war-making, immigration and virtually every other government function. Trump is hardly the first president to try to sharply elbow the other branches out of the way.

In 1981, Ronald Reagan startled critics by firing more than 11,000 air traffic controllers. George W. Bush, jolted by the terrorist attacks of Sept. 11, 2001, secretly approved tactics against prisoners that many considered torture.

Barack Obama, initially critical of such actions, went on to expand presidential authority in his own right. He created the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program in 2012 by executive order, prompting GOP complaints that he was simply making up a law. He used drone strikes to target and kill suspected terrorists far from traditional battlefields. And he put numerous “czars” over areas like energy and health care, which Republicans charged was a way to avoid confirmation fights.

Tiffany Justice, executive vice president of the conservative group Heritage Action, pointed to this history to dismiss talk of post-Trump reforms, saying the president is doing nothing Democratic presidents have not done and predicting that Democrats’ plans will go nowhere.

“They are full of baloney - I don’t think Democrats would ever limit the power of a Democratic president,” Justice said. “The idea of Democrats saving democracy, it’s nonsense.”

Administration officials argue that Trump has changed the country forever and followed established procedures for everything he has done. “The Trump administration has abided by all legal decisions and gone through the appellate process with great success,” said a White House spokesman. “His successes on behalf of the American people will be imprinted upon the fabric of America and will be felt by every other White House that comes after him,” said White House communications director Steven Cheung.

But Trump’s critics say that in the scale, sweep and sheer aggressiveness of his actions - from demolishing the East Wing of the White House to pursuing legal actions against political opponents - Trump has pushed executive authority far beyond any previous modern president.

With a possible recapture of Congress just one month away, Democrats’ efforts to limit the staying power of those changes are heating up.

Several lawmakers are crafting bills to curtail a president’s ability to declare emergencies, which Trump has used in novel ways, declaring about a dozen emergencies to justify policies as varied as imposing tariffs, accelerating deportations and deploying the National Guard. Reps. Suzan DelBene (D-Washington) and Don Beyer (D-Virginia) have introduced a bill forbidding a president from levying tariffs under the guise of a national emergency unless Congress agrees.

Raskin has drafted bills to ban a president from accepting payments from foreign governments without Congress’s consent and require a public review for renovations of the White House. Another measure would block a president from entering monetary settlements with his own government, which a federal judge scolded Trump and the Justice Department for this summer, saying they had attempted to “use” and “manipulate” the court to legitimize a deal that would have shielded Trump from IRS scrutiny and set up a nearly $1.8 billion fund for alleged victims of politicized prosecutions.

Rahm Emanuel, the former Chicago mayor and potential Democratic presidential candidate, recently released an ethics proposal for all three branches of government that would ban trading stocks and betting in prediction markets, require a blind trust for anyone worth more than $1 million, and forbid individuals from accepting foreign gifts. Trump has traded millions of dollars worth of individual stocks since taking office and famously accepted the gift of an aircraft from the Qatari government.

And Sen. Chris Murphy (D-Connecticut) has introduced a No Political Enemies Act, forbidding executive branch officials from prosecuting or punishing individuals or groups for their speech, something Trump has done relatively openly.

Some of these proposals may be partly symbolic, aimed at galvanizing voters and showing resistance to Trump rather than serving as strict blueprints for reform. Democrats themselves do not know when, if ever, they may have the public support to push them through. They have no guarantee of success; Trump survived two impeachments, prosecutions and investigations before winning the White House a second time.

Still, the Democrats say they see little alternative to trying.

The Partnership for Public Service, which trains government employees and advocates for ways to improve the public workforce, has crafted proposals to strengthen civil service protections, making it harder for future presidents to fire employees en masse as Trump and his ally Elon Musk did. Congress, for example, could strengthen rules requiring that hiring and firing must be based on merit and due process - and then confront an administration that violates those rules.

Would-be reformers argue that periods of excess in U.S. history often prompt waves of reform. The Gilded Age of the late 1800s gave way to the Progressive Era. The corruption of Watergate in the 1970s generated a slew of new ethics laws.

It is not clear whether Americans support a new wave of reform laws. But a Pew poll last year found that 78 percent of Americans had concerns about expanding presidential power.

“Throughout American history, reform follows scandal,” said Michael Waldman, president of the Brennan Center for Justice at New York University, a liberal-leaning think tank that focuses on law and democracy. “It does not always follow scandal, but that’s when it happens. I think there will be a real hunger, I hope from both parties, to write into law some of the protections that were assumed to be there before.”

Some historians say many of Trump’s actions will be hard to reverse. It is far easier to smash through guardrails, they say, than to rebuild them. Most modern presidents have expanded executive power at the expense of Congress. Whether that trend continues could depend in large part on whether the legislative branch begins to reassert itself as a counterweight to the presidency.

“Once we get through this nightmare, the rest of our careers will have to be devoted to reviving American progress and building institutions that endure and succeed,” Raskin said. “That is going to be the work of the rest of our lives.”

The temptation for revenge - or acquiescence

The midterm campaigns have spawned numerous Democratic candidates with sharply combative anti-Trump messages. If they win majorities in Congress, some Democrats could well be tempted to turn the president’s hardball tactics against him and his followers once he leaves the scene.

A post-Trump president could, for example, prod the Justice Department to investigate his own political adversaries, as Trump has.

“It will be very tempting for Democrats to say, ‘Oh, you think we are going to limit our abuse of the Justice Department? We don’t want to be suckers,’” Waldman said. “But I think that would be a big mistake. Everybody benefits when the rule of law is in play across the government.”

More immediately, the next administration will have to decide whether to prosecute Trump officials who may have broken the law by misusing their authority. Some Democrats, for example, say the way Justice Department officials have targeted Trump’s enemies is illegal and could expose those officials to charges.

Trump, in an effort to counteract such moves, has promised that before he leaves office he will preemptively pardon anyone who has come “within 200 feet” of the Oval Office, the Wall Street Journal has reported.

Some liberals say Democrats should take a lesson from Trump on how to govern with force and purpose. Trump does not hesitate to take actions that skirt the edges of legality, happy to let the courts sort it out. He pressures private firms to back his policies. He issues sweeping executive orders rather than trying to persuade Congress to act.

“This president litigates the way he bargains: He makes some very far-out claims, not expecting to win them all, but sort of ‘what the hell’ - that’s his theory,” said William A. Galston, a former domestic policy adviser to President Bill Clinton. “If you lose cases no other president would have dreamed of bringing, and you win a few big ones, you’re ahead of the game.”

It may be tempting for future presidents to act the same way. “There has been an overcautiousness in some Democratic and some Republican administrations that will seem quite quaint after this administration,” said Ben Olinsky, senior vice president at the Center for American Progress, a center-left think tank.

That is especially true of executive orders and actions, which Trump has refashioned as all-purpose policy and communications weapons. He has issued more than 280 so far in his second term, far outpacing his recent predecessors, according to figures compiled by the American Presidency Project at the University of California at Santa Barbara.

“A new administration will do a lot of governing through executive order,” said Richard Pildes, a constitutional law professor at New York University. “They will want to show that they can act decisively.”

Even while they plot a post-Trump future, many Democrats say they cannot simply return to a status quo that voters hated. Yet it is far from clear what their new agenda will be.

Max Stier, president of the nonpartisan Partnership for Public Service, said the damage Trump has inflected on the current system opens up new possibilities. Stier has suggested slashing the roughly 4,000 political appointees in the government, saying they can be unqualified and unaccountable.

“There is opportunity in this madness, the opportunity to reexamine some of the basic expectations around our government,” Stier said. “Because the status quo has been disrupted, the ability to think larger and bigger is there.”

Tiffany Justice, of Heritage Action, challenged that entire narrative. Trump is not wielding the presidency in some new way, she said, but rather using it as Democrats always have - and that is what truly upsets the left.

“President Trump is using his power in a way that Democrats have in the past,” Justice said, citing, for example, President Joe Biden’s order protecting gender transition care. “Republicans always in the past have been uneasy about using power. Democrats are never uneasy about using power.”

Another Watergate?

If there is anything that gives would-be reformers hope, it is the aftermath of the Watergate scandal that brought down President Richard M. Nixon.

Nixon, like Trump, stretched presidential authority in ways that challenged the law and the Constitution. After his 1974 resignation, a previously quiescent Congress roared back to action, as lawmakers rushed to make sure Watergate could not happen again. Congress passed bills restricting a president’s ability to misuse private data, spy on Americans, misspend campaign cash, declare emergencies, control spending and more.

Some critics envision a post-Trump America swept up in a similar reform fever, with lawmakers scrambling to score political points amid widespread public revulsion over Trump’s self-aggrandizement and self-enrichment.

For example, Congress could make it illegal to do what Trump’s firebrand housing official Bill Pulte has done - accuse the president’s critics of mortgage fraud with little evidence. Or it could restrict the ability of a Federal Communications Commission chairman, like Trump’s Brendan Carr, to target outlets disliked by the president.

The Justice Department is a particular focus of the would-be reformers, many of them former department lawyers frustrated by the way Trump has used DOJ to pursue his adversaries. Under Attorney General Todd Blanche, formerly Trump’s personal attorney, and his predecessor Pam Bondi, many experienced attorneys have fled the department or been forced out.

Vanita Gupta, who served as associate attorney general under Biden, said Justice Department veterans of both parties are discussing how to restore the department to its former ethos of independence.

“Rebuilding will be challenging, no doubt, but former DOJ officials from Republican and Democratic administrations are already thinking about how to get it done,” Gupta said. “Seasoned career leaders have told me that they would return to rebuild the department, even knowing lifetime tenure may be a thing of the past.”

Historians concede the Watergate analogy has its limits. The 1974 scandal propelled Democrats to overwhelming majorities of 61-39 in the Senate and 291-144 in the House; those margins are unthinkable today. Americans have become more polarized in the past 50 years, a trend that works against any broad-based reform crusade.

A powerful executive has gained additional theoretical backing in recent decades, as conservative legal scholars have advanced a “unitary executive” theory, arguing the U.S. Constitution gives the president nearly unfettered, unreviewable control over the executive branch.

What the people want

Ultimately, the shape of the post-Trump future will be determined by how Americans feel when he exits the stage: Will they applaud his exercise of power and attacks on long-standing structures? Or will they recoil?

“The president and the courts are staring at one another over the mostly supine body of the Congress of the United States, and it’s very dangerous for constitutional government,” Galston said.

The Supreme Court’s path is unclear as well. Some Democrats privately echo a sentiment voiced by Clinton - that the justices may not give future presidents the same leeway they have accorded Trump. The court has already been far more deferential to Trump than it was to Biden, these Democrats say.

“I have a sinking suspicion if our party wins the White House in the next election, there will be a hallelujah moment and the Supreme Court will rediscover the Constitution,” Clinton said on ABC’s “The View” last year.

Even if some curbs on presidential power are reestablished, Trump’s demonstration that they can be dismantled is likely to have long-term effects.

Young people might be less willing to work for a government whose policies vacillate wildly from one president to another, and where long tenure is not guaranteed. Foreign allies have made it clear they are far less trusting of Washington’s commitments. Businesses and nonprofits could be less interested in accepting funding they fear could be abruptly withdrawn.

“It’s not like a toggle switch that you can just turn it on and off,” Waldman said. “Much of the federal government took a century to build.”

Some historians note Trump’s unique qualities, saying his combination of celebrity, aggressiveness and disregard for tradition is unlikely ever to be replicated. That suggests future presidents cannot simply repeat his performance, they say.

“Any thought that [Vice President] JD Vance or [Secretary of State] Marco Rubio gets to be president and do the same thing with the same abandon - I don’t see that happening,” said John Lawrence, a historian and former top aide to former House speaker Nancy Pelosi (D-California). “He has created his own unitary executive theory, and I don’t know how it works outside the size and force of the personality of Donald Trump. But that doesn’t mean a Republican successor wouldn’t try.”

In the Progressive Era, Americans took to the streets by the thousands to demand reform, Stier said, and if Trump’s changes are ultimately reversed, it will be because of a similar groundswell.

“The most important question we face is whether we can return to a consensus that we had among Republicans, Democrats and independents for 140 years that an operating government of our values requires leaders committed to the public good, not the private interests of the officeholder of the day,” Stier said. “Can we get back to that? I think the answer is yes. But we need a public that demands it.”

Related Content

This article originally appeared on Washington Post at https://washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/10/04/democrats-are-making-plans-clean-up-government-post-trump-era/

item.title: 大风！降温！冷空气“冻”真格了
item.description:
今明两天（10月4日至5日），冷空气影响我国中东部，多地气温将创新低，凉意加重。同时，南方降雨将减少、减弱，后天大部地区降雨基本停歇，但夜间降温明显。


冷空气影响我国中东部
多地气温将创新低

今明天，冷空气继续东移南下影响中东部多地。中央气象台预计，华北、黄淮、江汉等地先后有4至6级偏北风，阵风7至9级，高海拔山区局地10级以上，气温下降4℃至6℃，局地降幅可达8℃至10℃。

降温过后，东北地区多地最高气温将在15℃以下，西北地区东部、华北在20℃左右。城市中，长春、沈阳、北京、天津今天最高气温或将创立秋后新低。

随着冷空气南下，叠加阴雨影响，南方不少地方最高气温也会逐渐下探，并创立秋后新低。今天，西南地区东部到江南多地最高气温仅在20℃上下，华南一带30℃以上的区域也会明显缩减。

随着降雨消减，南方大部夜间辐射降温明显，明起至7日最低气温将会大范围创新低，像福州、广州、南宁等城市最低气温都会跌破20℃，为立秋后首次，南京、合肥等地仅10℃左右，早晚需注意添衣。

南方降雨今天起减少减弱
后天基本停歇

今天，南方降雨将减少、减弱，明后天降雨将逐渐停歇。北方今明天降水主要出现在东北等地。具体来看——

  • 今天，西藏东南部、川西高原南部和四川南部、云南南部、贵州东南部、湖南南部、广西北部和南部、广东大部、海南岛、福建大部、浙江南部、辽宁东部、吉林东部和南部等地部分地区有中到大雨，其中，吉林东部、云南南部、广西北部、广东南部、海南岛等地部分地区有暴雨。

  • 明天，黑龙江东南部、吉林东部、新疆北部、西藏东南部、四川南部、云南西部、海南岛、台湾岛北部和东部等地部分地区有中到大雨，其中，吉林东部、云南西南部、海南岛中东部、台湾岛北部和东部等地部分地区有暴雨。

  • 后天，四川南部、云南西部、海南岛东南部等地部分地区有中到大雨，其中，云南西南部等地部分地区有暴雨。


提醒公众，南方今天降雨将有所减弱，但地质灾害具有滞后性，贵州、湖南等地前期累计降雨量大，需防范山洪、滑坡等次生灾害的发生；正值国庆假期，公众需注意避雨防滑，出行请留意交通安全。

item.title: 女子将挎包遗落在休息椅上，包里装有十多万元现金，列车开行数分钟后才发现，工作人员紧急寻回，铁路部门提示
item.description:
“真的太惊喜、太感动了！
包里装着十多万元的现金
发现包弄丢之后我彻底慌了
没想到东站工作人员
这么负责、效率这么高
一分不少帮我找回来了！”

10月3日14时许
成都东站失物招领处内
旅客席女士手持锦旗
紧紧握着工作人员的手
言语间满是激动与由衷的感激


国庆假期，铁路迎来出行客流高峰。10月2日19时许，成都东站新入路职工徐涛在巡视站台途中，发现12站台中部休息椅上放置着一个无人看管的黑色挎包。考虑到包内物品未知、存在财物遗失风险，他第一时间联系自己的师傅、客运员陈旭元到现场处置。

陈旭元接到通知后迅速赶往现场，途中同步将该遗失物品情况上报客运值班主任安宇宵及车站派出所民警。安宇宵与民警抵达现场后，对挎包进行开包查验。经仔细清点核查，包内装有人民币及多种外币等贵重财物，总价值折合人民币十多万元。


为尽快联系上失主，安宇宵当即通知车站综控室循环播报寻物广播，寻找失主线索，并联合派出所民警将挎包送至成都东站遗失物品招领处，由专人保管。

就在站内全力寻人之际，失物招领处值班员卓悦收到了旅客通过12306平台提交的寻物求助工单。她迅速比对信息、仔细核实细节，锁定提交工单的席女士就是该黑色挎包的失主。

随后，卓悦第一时间与席女士取得联系。原来，席女士因随身携带行李较多，候车途中在站台中部休息椅短暂落座，登车时一时疏忽，将装有大额财物的挎包遗落在休息椅上。列车开行数分钟后，她才发现挎包遗失，心急如焚，向列车工作人员说明情况，并在列车工作人员引导下通过12306客服热线提交寻物工单，向成都东站寻求帮助。


“您不要着急，慢慢来，挎包已经妥善保管好了。”卓悦温柔细致的安抚，让身处异地、满心焦虑的席女士彻底放下心来。席女士随即告知工作人员，将在次日从外地返回成都东站领取失物。

10月3日14时，席女士来到成都东站失物招领处，看着失而复得的财物，她激动不已，再三向车站工作人员致谢，并用锦旗表达自己最真挚的谢意。

铁路部门温馨提示：

旅客在出行时，请务必妥善看护好随身行李、手机、钱包等贵重物品。如若在旅途中不慎遗失物品，切勿慌张，可第一时间通过12306服务热线提交求助，铁路工作人员将全力协助查找，用心守护广大旅客平安、舒心出行。

item.title: 内蒙古阿尔山通报“两百一晚简陋大酒店”
item.description:
澎湃新闻记者 王鑫

针对短视频平台有网友反映“阿尔山景区二百一晚的大酒店”，内蒙古阿尔山市市场监督管理局于10月4日晚发布通报称，视频拍摄地点为当地居民包某某自有住宅，当事人未办理营业执照私自对外提供住宿接待服务，构成无照经营的违法行为。视频所称“大酒店”，系网友戏谑调侃表述，当事人自身并未使用该名称对外宣传推广。

网友发布的“阿尔山景区二百一晚的大酒店”视频截图。

经调查核实，本次接待对象为随团陪同司机，入住前曾请求当事人为其联系多家宾馆、民宿均无空房，遂推荐自家居住房屋，入住前当事人已如实告知房屋设施简陋、居住条件较差的实际情况，双方协商达成一致，确定住宿费用为100元/人/晚，并于入住当晚为其提供免费餐食。该场所无OTA线上宣传经营渠道，未发现价格欺诈、虚假宣传等价格违法行为。

澎湃新闻注意到，某网友于3天前发布的该视频时长21秒，为第一人称视角拍摄，网友打开房门后为厨房，厨房旁为一间卧室，卧室内的炕上铺着白色的床单和枕头。截至发稿前，该条视频转发量达19.6万，点赞4.9万，评论近万条。

通报称，针对无照从事住宿经营的违法行为，执法人员现场进行问询取证，依据《市场主体登记管理条例》第四十三条规定，责令当事人立即停止住宿接待经营活动，同时对当事人现场开展普法宣传教育，告知从事经营性住宿服务，须依法办理市场主体登记，并取得公共场所卫生等法定许可后方可开展经营。该场所环境卫生、布草保洁等卫生相关线索，同步移送卫生健康综合行政执法部门处置；相关线索同时推送文旅主管部门，提醒旅行社严禁安排人员入住无资质私人住宅。

item.title: 9月香港一手住宅成交达三个月高位：新盘开盘即售罄，有人️连买4套
item.description:
澎湃新闻记者 计思敏

随着新房推盘节奏重新加快，9月香港楼市显著回暖。

中原地产研究部数据显示，9月，香港整体楼宇买卖合约登记(包括住宅、车位及工商铺物业)录6440宗，较8月上升11.7%。

中原地产研究部高级联席董事杨明仪指出，8月港股走势平稳，九龙新盘以贴近二手市价推售，市场反应热烈带动整体楼市气氛；同时，多家大型银行延续定息按揭优惠计划，买家恢复入市意愿，整体成交终止连续两个月的回落走势。

其中，受长沙湾新盘热销带动，9月一手私人住宅成交重回千宗以上水平，成交宗数与金额双双创下今年6月以来的三个月高位。据中原地产研究部数据，9月，香港一手私人住宅合约登记录得1500宗、总值208.8亿港元，环比分别上涨61.6%及73.0%。

公开信息显示，9月，华润置地海外发展旗下西南九龙项目叡璟Ⅱ推出的153套房源开盘即售罄，其中4组大手客（“大手客”指同一买家在同一时间于同一楼盘购入多套房源的客户‌）均购入4套房源。随后，开发商加推129套房源再获全数沽清。此外，香港北角熙和街项目皇璇项目同样掀起认购热潮。

受新房热卖带动，二手房市场同步企稳。数据显示，9月二手私人住宅买卖合约登记3029宗，总值247.6亿港元，环比分别上升11.4%及10.3%。

从季度表现来看，整体受开发商减慢推盘影响，中原地产研究部监测，今年第三季度，香港一手私宅累计登记3196宗及487.9亿港元，按季分别下跌54.0%、43.2%；二手私人住宅第三季登记宗数跌36.5%。

美联集团行政总裁暨美联物业执行董事马泰阳表示，香港楼市经历上半年房价及成交明显上升后，自6月下旬起进入短暂的整固期，一、二手交投速度有所放缓，房价升势亦明显放缓。不过，随着新房推盘节奏重新加快，买家及投资者正逐步重返市场。

马泰阳指出，回顾过去香港楼市周期，市场多次呈现“成交升—后整固—再发力”的发展模式。其中，2003年-2007年、2015年-2017年两个阶段，楼市均有类似发展：市场首先受需求回升及楼市气氛改善影响，成交量逐步增加；其后房价加快上扬，业主叫价与买家预期出现短暂落差，导致成交量进入整固期。待市场适应新的价格水平后，买家重新建立入市信心，成交量再度回升。现时楼市同样呈现“成交先升、其后整固”的阶段性特征。在多项利好因素叠加及新盘气氛带动下，楼市有望完成整固后重回上升轨道。

从房价表现来看，香港差饷物业估价署9月28日发布的数据显示，香港8月房价指数止跌回升，报320.5，按月升0.06%；按年升近11%。

马泰阳指出，目前香港房价较2021年历史高位仍有落差，存在一定的“追落后”空间。其预计，第四季度房价有望重回上升轨道，单季升幅扩大至近4%，并维持全年房价上升约15%的预测。

此外，香港富豪对楼市信心不减。据美联物业研究中心数据，9月(截至28日)逾亿元超级豪宅一手成交量录达30宗，较8月全月15宗高出约1倍，并打破今年1月26宗的纪录高位，创自2013年一手销售条例实施以来的单月新高。

值得一提的是，租赁市场的表现，也成为当前香港楼市重要支撑。美联物业分析师岑颂谦表示，在传统租赁旺季及人才持续流入带动下，香港住宅租金屡创新高。

美联物业研究中心数据显示，8月香港私人住宅实用面积平均呎租达40.88港元，按月上升0.81%，实现连续8个月上涨，今年首8个月累计升约5.55%。岑颂谦认为，人口增长叠加专才、人才及家属来港定居、留学生持续赴港，均对租赁市场带来极大支持，租金持续走高亦促使部分租房群体加速转向置业市场。


本期编辑 陆枫

item.title: 最短间隔40秒，冲上热搜！网友：不愧是“宇宙第一大站”
item.description:
这个国庆假期
广州南站的发车密度
又一次引发网友热议
登上热搜榜单

最短40秒的发车间隔
让网友直呼
“不愧是‘宇宙第一大站’”
 “广州南站不语，只是一味发车”
“这是把高铁当地铁开”


热议的背后
是一份创下历史纪录的运营数据——
10月1日
广州南站到发旅客达104.9万人次


运能拉满
“一日一图” 加开列车

广州南站站场规模为15台28线，京广高铁、贵广高铁、南广高铁、广深港高铁等多条线路在此交会，是全国高铁网的重要枢纽节点。


从广州南站开出的列车可直达全国23个省级行政区、196座城市。


为应对国庆假期大客流，广州南站实行“一日一图”，动态调整列车开行方案，采取加开高峰线列车、开行夜间高铁、重联动车组等方式，提升去往深圳、长沙、南宁、珠海、郑州、重庆等方向的运能。


10月1日，广州南站开行营业列车1252列，其中夜间高铁202列，高峰时段最短发车间隔仅40秒。

item.title: “亚运会银牌，回家也得掰苞米”
item.description:
10月3日下午，在亚运会摘得历史性银牌的女子田径选手李春辉发视频称：亚运银牌回家也得掰苞米。


视频画面显示，李春辉身穿黑色运动套装，戴着手套坐在玉米堆前熟练地掰着苞米。评论区有网友调侃道：“难怪亚运会要在九月份办，是怕耽误秋收”“怪不得跑那么快，原来赶紧跑完回家收玉米”。还有网友称赞：既是国家的功臣，也是父母的女儿。



9月26日晚，名古屋亚运会田径女子1500米决赛赛场上，来自吉林通化的25岁选手李春辉，在终点线前完成对日本名将田中希实的超越，以4分05秒50的个人最好成绩摘得银牌。这也是中国选手时隔28年再次登上该项目领奖台。


10月3日晚，据媒体报道，李春辉经纪人表示，这次亚运会紧接着就是国庆节，李春辉结束比赛后刚好回家休息，“她在家就是日常生活，她从小非常懂事，经常帮父母干活。家人对她走田径这条路也很支持。”后续她再休息几天就会归队训练，为下次比赛做准备，“下一步就是准备明年的世锦赛，虽然难度很大，但也会努力争取拿奖牌。”


李春辉 资料图 来源：新华社


公开信息显示，李春辉出生于2001年，吉林省通化人。2012年，12岁的她在一次运动会上被通化市体育运动学校教练员张吉国慧眼识珠，开启了正规田径中长跑项目训练。2016年，李春辉首次参加全国比赛——全国青少年锦标赛，并一举成名，斩获800米、1500米双料冠军。


此后，李春辉夺得多项国内及亚洲赛事的800米及1500米冠军，并成功入选国家队。近几年，她连续多次称霸国内各大赛事，逐步确立了国内女子中长跑项目的领先地位。

item.title: 停止做这4件事，血管就能老得慢一点
item.description:
生活中我们会发现，年纪相仿的人，有些看起来年轻，有些会比较显老，人们的血管也是如此。


同龄人中，有的人血管壁光滑，有的可能早早出现动脉粥样硬化斑块、血管狭窄，甚至血管闭塞等症状。


《生命时报》综合多位专家观点，总结让血管提前变老的生活习惯，并告诉你不同人群多久应该查一次心血管。


4个伤血管的日常习惯


一般来说，血管会随着年龄增长逐渐老化，但受到很多因素影响，血管会提前变老。


久坐不动

人体血液循环很大程度依靠肌肉收缩助推，久坐后，全身肌肉会处于松弛停滞状态，血液流速明显减慢，血管损伤会随久坐时长而持续加重。


久坐1小时，下肢血液流速可减慢20%以上，血液黏稠度升高；久坐3小时，血管舒张能力可下降30%，血管壁逐渐僵硬、变脆；久坐8小时，血管会进入“早衰受损状态”，血管硬化、狭窄速度加快，下肢静脉血栓风险飙升。



建议：每坐40~60分钟，应起身活动3~5分钟。坐着时也可通过踮脚勾脚、扩胸拉伸等动作，来促进血液循环。静坐时不要跷二郎腿、瘫坐塌腰，同时要少量、多次喝温水。


偏爱高脂饮食

高脂食物会在短时间内推高甘油三酯和血糖水平，同时导致胰岛素激增，这些变化会直接损伤血管内皮。


内皮受损后，体内会产生大量炎症因子和氧化应激物质，最终导致血管功能下降。原本有弹性的血管壁变得僵硬，使血管的舒张能力下降，心脏和大脑也会得不到足够的血液供应。


建议：


  • 购买食物时看食品标签，尤其关注“脂肪”和“饱和脂肪”含量；


  • 脂肪来源优先选择深海鱼、坚果等富含不饱和脂肪的食物；


  • 尽量减少煎、烤、炸等高油的烹调方式，多采用蒸、煮、炖等健康的烹饪方法；


  • 注意食材的处理，如去除肉类可见的肥膘、给禽肉去皮、喝汤前撇去浮油等。


作息不规律

首都医科大学附属北京积水潭医院心血管内科主任医师王佐岩介绍，若长期作息不规律，大脑和身体器官之间会产生“时差”。这会让身体误以为处于持续应激状态，交感神经系统被迫全天候兴奋，释放大量肾上腺素。



这不仅会导致血管持续痉挛、血压升高，还会破坏血管内皮的自我修复功能，加速动脉粥样硬化斑块形成。


建议：每天在固定时间上床和起床，即使是周末和假期，偏差也不要超过30~60分钟。尽量在22~23时入睡，保证7~9小时睡眠时间。


起床后尽早接触自然光，告诉大脑“白天开始了”；睡前2小时尽量远离手机和电脑的蓝光，让身体自然分泌褪黑素。


抽烟饮酒

包括二手烟在内的所有形式烟草，都会导致炎症、内皮功能障碍，严重损害心血管健康。


酒精也对心血管健康无益，还会增加患高血压性心脏病、心肌病、房颤、脑卒中等疾病的风险。


建议：不沾染任何形式的烟草，包括电子烟，并避免被动吸二手烟和三手烟。


建议尽量不喝酒，常喝酒的人从少喝酒做起。成年男性每天酒精摄入量最好小于25克，女性小于15克。


护血管，还要做好6件事


除了规避以上不良习惯，首都医科大学附属北京安贞医院心脏超声医学中心副主任医师牛宝荣，推荐了几个能改善心血管代谢健康的生活秘诀。


瘦腰增肌

在护心方面，减脂增肌比单纯减重更重要。国人腹型肥胖偏多，减腰围格外重要，男性应将腰围减小到90厘米以下，女性减小到85厘米以下。


养成运动习惯

建议每周运动3~5次，每次至少运动30~60分钟，可轮流进行有氧、力量、灵活性和平衡运动。运动一定要量力而行，根据自身情况循序渐进，最终养成规律运动的习惯。



尝试间歇性禁食

在营养均衡的基础上实行间歇性禁食或限时进食，有助管理体重和改善代谢。


  • 超重的人，吃饭最多八分饱；

  • 尽量在8~10小时的时间窗内摄入食物，少吃零食；

  • 吃饭时全身心投入，尽量不看手机和电视。


学会释放压力

慢性精神压力和持续的负面情绪，会显著影响心血管健康。


可通过正念冥想和缓慢的深呼吸来帮助减压，如每天进行45分钟瑜伽、冥想或太极拳等，还可以通过学习新技能或培养爱好，保持终身学习的状态来刺激大脑。


增加社交互动

缺乏社会和情感支持会增加患心血管疾病的风险。建议多和家人、朋友沟通，建立深厚联系，和平友好地与别人相处。


尽量每周至少2次有意义的面对面交谈；每两周1次团体活动，比如合唱、广场舞、志愿者活动；每月1次老友、亲戚聚会。


亲近大自然

多亲近大自然，空气严重污染时，应减少户外活动或外出佩戴口罩。


普通人多久查一次心血管？


《柳叶刀·区域健康（西太平洋）》发表的一项由北京大学公共卫生学院等机构学者开展的研究建议，我国30~79岁成年人中：


  • 低风险人群：每6年进行一次心血管风险评估；

  • 中低风险人群：每3年进行一次心血管风险评估；

  • 中高风险人群：每2年全面检查一次。




低风险人群通常是心血管疾病风险因素较少的个体，一般年龄偏低，血压、血脂正常且无糖尿病，没有吸烟习惯等。


中低风险人群可能有少量的心血管风险因素，包括高血压、血脂轻度升高、处于糖尿病前期等。


中高风险人群则存在多个心血管病危险因素，比如高血压、血脂明显升高、糖尿病、长期吸烟等。





北京大学第一医院心内科副主任医师王洁建议，不同心血管疾病风险人群可采取以下筛查项目。


低风险人群

推荐筛查项目包括血压、血脂、空腹血糖、以及心电图等。建议平时通过维持健康的生活方式，以预防高血压、高脂血症和糖尿病。


中低风险人群

除了上述低风险人群的基础评估项目外，中低风险人群还可视情况检测糖化血红蛋白、脉搏波传导速度和踝肱指数等。


平时建议积极控制已知危险因素，除生活方式干预外，必要时遵医嘱开展药物干预。


中高风险人群

在上述中低风险人群评估项目的基础上，建议这类人群视情况增加超声心动图、冠状动脉钙化积分、颈动脉超声等影像学检查。


防控重点是在生活方式干预的基础上，及时通过药物强化控制血压、血糖、血脂，并在医生指导下适时启动抗血小板治疗，以预防心血管事件发生。

item.title: 中国人民大学：收到一位校友5.03亿元捐赠
item.description:
“中国人民大学”微信公号

从“新中国新大学”到“新时代新校园”，以新布局构建新格局，以新空间助力走新路。

近期，中国人民大学收到一位校友5.03亿元捐赠，用于支持母校通州校区体育中心建设。

体育中心是通州校区重要标志性建筑之一，在设计时提取陕北公学时期标志性“窑洞”元素，彰显校园文化脉络，以玉兰花造型和元素贯穿其中，营造“一树玉兰”的雅致意境，以连续人字形曲线窗，凝炼“人民、人本、人文”的精神内核，一砖一瓦，皆见来路，一梁一柱，恒久传承。

西立面效果图

 北立面效果图

体育中心总建筑面积约4.2万平方米，集篮球、羽毛球、网球、乒乓球、游泳、攀岩、健身等各类室内运动场地于一体，突出“专业、智慧、健康”设计理念和建筑特色，具备承办全国性综合赛事和国际单项赛事条件，功能多元，文体兼顾，可高效实现专业体育赛事模式，与日常教学、训练模式的快速切换，为师生提供高品质校园公共空间。

item.title: 连续推出多型主战装备，越南军工崛起缘何“突然崛起”
item.description:
澎湃新闻特约撰稿 兰顺正

近日，越南开建3000吨级护卫舰和自研主战坦克的新闻引发了外界对越南军工“崛起”的关注。

越南T-1两栖轻型坦克，仿制PT-76坦克。

长久以来，越南国防工业在东南亚的标签长期是“装备维修、弹药仿制、轻武器组装”。从越南战争结束后数十年，越军主力装备大多继承苏式旧装备，现代化主力舰艇、主战坦克、导弹高度依赖外购，本土军工企业的核心业务仅停留在装备大修、零部件替换与轻武器生产层面。因此，越南军工给人留下的长久印象是只能生产制造一些轻武器和弹药，整体实力比较弱小。

但近几年来，越南国防工业发生了不小的变化，不但在之前陆续推出国产两栖坦克、轮式步兵战车、多型无人机、VCM-01系列反舰导弹等，近期还在岘港秋河造船厂开工建造 3000吨级国产中型多功能反潜护卫舰，并正式启动了T-2第三代主战坦克研发项目。

这一系列重大项目接连落地，标志着越南军工正在从“修修补补”的后勤保障阶段，逐步跨入主战装备自主设计、集成制造的新阶段。那么，越南军工发展现状如何？底色又是如何？

越南XCB-01履带式步兵战车参考了 BMP-1 的设计，外形也非常相似。

步兵战车、反舰导弹……连续推出多型主战装备

首先，我们来看看，越南国防工业近年来推出了哪些主战装备。

在陆军装甲装备方面，今年6月越南军方正式公开展示首款自主研发的T-1两栖轻型坦克原型车。该型坦克基于越南现役苏制PT-76B两栖坦克理念迭代研发，整体全面升级。相较于PT-76B，该车车身加长，每侧负重轮由6个增至7个，整车增重约4吨，车辆搭载470马力柴油发动机，公路最高时速可达80公里。T-1采用双人炮塔，标配76毫米自动装填火炮，辅以同轴机枪。该坦克核心优势为全域两栖通行能力，填补了重型主战坦克无法适配水网区域作战的短板，适配越南本土地形防御作战和两栖作战需求，用于提升越军地面部队复杂地形战术灵活性。

8 月，越南又公开了国产XTC03八轮两栖装甲战车实车影像，展示原型车陆地机动、水上浮渡航行能力。该车由越南Z111工厂负责总装研制，是越南首款本土设计的8×8轮式装甲战斗车辆，炮塔借鉴BMP2步兵战车武器系统，采用前置发动机布局，乘员编制3人，可搭载 8 名全副武装步兵，车尾开设步兵上下车舱门，重点适配越南国内河网、三角洲、滨海两栖作战环境。XTC-03战斗全重约16吨，搭载30毫米机关炮、7.62 毫米并列机枪与国产观瞄火控系统，车体正面可抵御 14.5 毫米穿甲弹，侧面主要防御 7.62 毫米机枪弹与炮弹破片。

越南XTC-03步兵战车，实际上是俄罗斯BTR-80步兵战车的“拉皮”版本。

之后在9月8日，越南国防部副部长范怀南上将宣告，越南主战坦克自研自产计划正式启动，代号T-2。相关报道指出，T-2以俄罗斯的T-90S主战坦克为蓝本，采用焊接炮塔布局、经典苏式车体构型，配备“窗帘”-1红外干扰系统、分置的炮长和车长瞄准镜等。现役T-90S的维护体系、弹药储备和使用经验，都将直接赋能T-2的研发与后续列装。在火力方面，T-2极有可能采用125毫米2A46系列滑膛炮（越南Z125军工厂已在2025年完成了该型火炮身管的制造与测试），可以发射尾翼稳定脱壳穿甲弹、高爆榴弹以及激光制导的9M119“反射”炮射导弹，搭配越南军用电子电信公司研发的S-FCS数字化火控系统，具备挑战第三代主战坦克的实力。

海上装备是越南军备更新的重点领域，其中反舰导弹是越南非对称海防作战的核心装备。2019年，越南利用在俄罗斯Kh-35E “天王星”导弹引进与生产时获得的解决方案与相关技术，启动了一款代号为“A1”的导弹研制计划，这款新型导弹被越南命名为VCM-01（越南巡航导弹01号）。VCM-01是一款亚音速巡航导弹，主要用于打击水面目标，其整体尺寸和重量与Kh-35E接近或相同，重量约600公斤，半穿甲弹头重量约145公斤，飞行速度约0.9马赫，可以在海面10米左右掠海飞行，动力系统很可能使用了韩国许可生产的三型SS-760K涡喷发动机，射程约300公里。同时VCM-01导弹也是一种多用途导弹，可以装备岸基、空基、海基多个发射平台。VCM-01的量产使越南具备独立生产中型亚音速反舰导弹的能力，不再完全依赖进口。

越南展示VCM-01的国产化反舰导弹，越南已经将该导弹集成在多艘老旧的舰艇上。

在主力舰艇方面，8月10日越南在岘港秋河造船厂举行国产中型多用途反潜护卫舰开工仪式，堪称越南军用造船史上标志性事件。该舰满载排水量约3000吨，基于“猎豹”级护卫舰放大改进而来，配备一体化桅杆、四面相控阵雷达。火炮武器基本上将是“猎豹”级方案的延续，包括舰首1门76毫米62倍径AK-176M舰炮和舰尾2门六管30毫米AK-630M舰炮。在反潜武器方面，该舰舰首甲板将配备2具12管RBU-6000火箭深弹发射装置，同时两侧舯部口盖内设有2座双联装533毫米鱼雷发射管。该舰舯部上层安装两座四联装VCM-01反舰导弹发射器。该舰舰艏楼甲板将安装2个垂直发射单元，各6个垂直发射管。军舰舰桥上还将搭载机枪座和双联装单兵导弹等辅助武器，尾部有直升机机库和甲板，可起降卡-28反潜直升机。

值得一提的是，受俄乌冲突的影响，越南正加快打造自己的无人作战力量，已形成涵盖长航时无人机、巡飞弹、反无人机系统及电子战装备的产品体系，并逐步进入国际防务市场。今年5月，越南军工企业Viettel在土耳其SAHA Expo 2026防务展上公开展示多款新型无人机与巡飞弹系统，包括VTUAV-M中程侦察无人机、VTUAV-S战术侦察平台以及VTUAV巡飞弹系统。 其中VTUAV-M为中程垂直起降侦察无人机，翼展约3.1米，机长约1.7米，最大起飞重量约26千克，采用“汽油发动机+四电动升力桨”混合动力布局，可在无跑道条件下自主起降，适用于前沿阵地、山地及岛礁等复杂地域部署。VTUAV-S则定位为战术级监视平台，重点执行边境巡逻、海岸监视与海上态势感知任务，可为越南海军、海警与边防部队提供低空持续侦察能力。VTUAV巡飞弹系统强调“侦察+打击”一体化运用，可在发现目标后实施自主攻击。

越南军工的“有限崛起”

越南拥有漫长海岸线与复杂的河口三角洲地形，海洋利益是其国家战略的核心组成部分。2026年7月28日，越共十四届三中全会颁布关于将越南建设和发展成为海洋强国的第20号决议，明确提出建设现代化海上力量，维护近海海洋权益，但周边国家海军力量的不断增强让越南感受到明显的装备代差压力，这直接倒逼其装备体系升级与国防工业自主化建设。

在陆军方面，越南陆军装甲部队规模位居东南亚前列，但装备老化问题极其突出。现役坦克中，大量 T-54/55、T-34 等老式苏制坦克仍在服役，仅有少量 T-90S 主战坦克从俄罗斯引进。老式坦克的火力、防护和机动性都已难以满足作战需求，而大规模外购主战坦克成本高昂，且受国际军贸合同限制，后续维护、零部件供应容易受制于人。

同时，过去数十年越南武器采购高度依赖俄罗斯，从潜艇、护卫舰、战机、坦克到导弹，俄式装备占据越军现代化装备主体。俄乌冲突爆发之后，俄罗斯军工产能被大量消耗，对外交付周期拉长，部分武器零部件出口受限。越南意识到，过度依赖单一国家作为装备供应源，会带来巨大战略风险。

另外外交战略的改变也产生了巨大影响。2016年8月，时任越南共产党中央委员会总书记阮富仲在全国对外工作会议上首先提出“竹式外交”概念，强调越南外交的坚韧性和灵活性。2021年拜登当选美国总统后，积极促进两国间多领域互动与合作，进而推动美越全面伙伴关系的深化发展。同时越美关系改善还促进了越南和印度、韩国等国的合作关系，进一步促进了越南军事合作关系的多元化，成为越南摆脱俄式武器依赖，进行军备转型的关键契机。

在此背景下，越南调整军贸策略，一方面继续维持与俄罗斯的传统军工合作，争取技术转让；另一方面积极拓展与以色列、韩国、印度、欧洲军工企业的合作渠道。这一策略保证了装备供应的稳定性与可持续性，也为本土国防工业吸收不同体系技术、提升自主研发能力创造了一定的条件。

越南国产3000吨级护卫舰模型首次亮相。

越南军工的短板与局限

尽管成果频出，但越南军工的“崛起”仍面临诸多难以逾越的障碍，核心在于工业基础的薄弱与体系集成能力的不足。

首先，越南军工的“国产化”更多是“全球采购+本土组装”。例如，T-2主战坦克的发动机、护卫舰的特种钢材与动力系统、无人机的核心芯片与传感器，均需依赖进口。越南武器装备的“国产化率”虽宣称很高，但关键设备如发动机、雷达、精密制导部件的核心技术却不在自己手中，一旦外部供应出现波动，装备生产就会停滞。

其次，越南过去长期只做装备维修、仿制、改装，完整自主设计三代主战坦克、中型护卫舰的经验几乎空白。T-2 坦克、中型护卫舰项目属于跨越式尝试，大量设计参考俄式成熟装备，创新程度低，项目延期、性能不达预期的可能性较大。而越南同时从俄、以、韩、欧洲多国引进不同标准的设备，不同国家装备的通信、数据总线、火控协议标准不一样，将多国硬件整合到同一台战车、同一艘军舰上，会出现数据兼容、电磁兼容等大量工程难题，增加系统调试难度，提升故障率。

另外，虽然越南军费逐年增长，但可以投入新型装备研发采购的资金依旧有限。主战坦克、中型护卫舰都是耗资巨大的项目，同时推进多个高端装备项目，会造成资源分散，量产规模大概率很小，难以形成大规模批量装备，成本很难摊薄。

长远来看，越南军工能够实现主战装备本土组装制造，减少外购成品装备数量，提升后勤自主保障能力，试图在东南亚区域军工竞争中占据一席之地，但在相当长一段时间内，难以脱离国外核心零部件供应，难以发展成完整独立的高端军工体系。


本期编辑 陆枫

item.title: 捡垃圾之乐
item.description:
来源: 
槽边往事

我认为世间没有所谓的「垃圾」，只存在价值错配。

如果你从这个角度去观察，世事就会变得有趣起来，不再局限在高级VS.低级，高档VS.垃圾这样的对立概念里。前几天我看到一条新闻，某位上海老教授去世之后，他的藏书被家人搬到楼下，一人两本大赠送。

老教授在世的时候，这些藏书都是他一本本精挑细选而来，选内容，选版本，选译者，视若珍宝，珍而藏之。然而，等到他驾鹤西归，这堆书对于家人来说，就是纯粹的占地方，一平方米的书，相当于要用几万块钱的空间去存放，所以赠送出去毫不心疼，只觉得如释重负。

之前我还在 Threads 上看到香港网友在垃圾房捡到了一堆金像奖小金人，上面还镌刻着某位著名制作人的名字。此公前几年去世，在世的时候很受业界尊重，荣膺无数奖项。结果，人去世之后，他的荣誉奖杯不知道是被盗还是被弃，当作垃圾直接扔掉。无论是哪种情况，很明显，在对方眼中这些承载曾经荣誉的奖杯不过是一些破铜烂铁，毫无价值。

而我自己前阵子在日本煤炉网站收了一些二手 CD，其中有几张是非常特别的版本，但售价和普通破烂没多大区别。卖家说自己售卖的所有物件都来自猝然逝世的大哥，继承下来之后，他既不喜欢这些东西，也根本不懂，所以上二手网站把它们全部尽快「处理」掉。我看了非常伤感，看看那些 CD 的名字和状态就知道，那位大哥生前花了多少时间精力去到处搜集，而且又花了多少心力去妥善保存。还好是落在了我手里，我会继续听下去。

你眼中的宝贝，可能正是他人眼中的垃圾；你眼中的垃圾，可能正是他人心头的珍宝。这就是我想说的：如果合适的东西都能配上合适的人，那世间就没有垃圾。对我自己来说，世界上有太多错配的东西，甚至包括生物和人，去所谓「垃圾」里发现价值，把它放回合适的位置，这会是很快乐的一件事。

上个月我买了一台蓝光 DVD 机，这年头人人都去看流媒体了，DVD 机尤其是二手货，价格就一再跳水。我买下来是为了播放 CD，根据国外宅男们的测试，我那一台各项播放指标非常优异，再看看它的价格，简直就是惊喜大礼包。

然而便宜货总是有问题：机器本身没有显示屏，不接电视机的话，我既不知道在播放 CD 上的哪一首，也不知道播放了多久。于是，我打算去给它接一个小显示器。然而，即便是杂牌的1K便携屏也要 200 左右。最后我找到了一款由老旧 iPad 屏改装的便携屏，2K 画质，100 出头。

目前，这套垃圾组合加上别人嘴里的「打口圆盘洋垃圾 CD」，正在我家里稳定播放。而且，我觉得它们配合得非常好。

如果我现在是十几岁，二十几岁，有人直言我是在玩「垃圾」，也许我会感到羞惭，感到焦虑。因为我也相信那一套叙事，要建立起高级和低级之间的壁垒，要努力从垃圾堆里节衣缩食伸手去够高档货。但我过了那个岁数，有人说我在玩垃圾，我会转身拉开帘子，骄傲地向他展示：不止这点，我还有更多垃圾，而且是成套、成建制的垃圾。

觉得是垃圾，我认为很合理，这是个人判断，但这种判断影响不到我，我也有我的一套。事实上，我很感激这些喜欢判定垃圾的人。如果不是他们那么坚决，我去哪里用很好的价格获得一本珍版书，一张发烧碟，以及一台性能优异但是廉价的 DVD 机？

垃圾是个刺耳的名词，不过在我的人生里，也曾经是某单位里的垃圾，而在另外一个单位则是亟待引进的人才。我还是我，不同的人眼里有不同的判断。一只被人遗弃的猫，落到另外一个人手里，或者一个让人避之不及的前任，遇见另外一颗心，故事的走向可能完全不同。

在个人能力范围内挑选最好的，这是一种选项。与此同时，在世界这个巨大的垃圾山上，选出别人扔掉但是自己喜欢的，这也是一种选择。两种选择不是非此即彼，前者是为了享受，为了减少麻烦，后者则是为了乐趣，为了找个折腾的理由。不过，我还是想多说一句：单一标准的「高级」，也许认同的人很多，但着实也有点无聊，因为它免除了你的个人判断。而你的个人判断和别人不同，在垃圾中找寻出价值来，这就要丰富、有趣得多。

衷心祝愿这个世界鱼找鱼，虾找虾，土豆找地瓜，蛤蟆找青蛙，我喜欢的都能到我家！

item.title: 做了四天杂工 体验底层普通男性
item.description:
来源: 
海兰珠阿婶

为体验底层普通男性的一天,在老家时也曾去钣金厂里做了四天杂工

主要工作就是在现场帮忙打扫铁屑，擦机器，帮忙抬 304 不锈钢板上划线机，再把划好线的不锈钢板拿去压槽机压出造型。而后转运给电焊车间，让他们焊接成型，最后再把成品送上车…

七月南昌三十几度，没有空调，没有恒温车间，老板就给准备了几台工业电扇对着工人吹。除了机器划线的时候能停个五分钟，剩下时间都在抬铁板运铁板收拾铁屑。每天下了班都热的我汗流浃背，双腿发软。回家时不光胸罩裤衩的能挤出水，全身都是汗味酸臭的，手无论洗几遍都有股铁味。

那工厂里一共 30 几个男的，多数单身。有几个还买了车。工厂包吃包住，四个人一个宿舍。厕所就在宿舍房入口，一走进宿舍房就能闻到一股子汗臭酸味混合着工装的味。

厂子里男的最小的 19 岁，07 年的，工资 3000，说想学个技术才去厂子上班，问他有对象吗？说不急。最老的单身汉 46 岁，80 年的，是成手大工，一个月六千来块，问他结过婚吗？老哥一笑，说找不到了，就自己一个人过了。

工厂是八小时工作制的。因为是私人小厂，订单少时一般都能五点下班。但有了订单就要大干特干。我是怎么了解到的呢？因为和厂里一干了很多年的老人聊，他说：为了赶订单加班到 10 点多是常态。我问他愿意加班吗？得到的答案很意外，与网上一帮见天强调八小时的不同… 那哥们笑了，说：全指望着加班赚钱，加班多的时候能多拿半个月的工资。没加班就五六千。

我干到最后一天，双腿发软，困乏已极，说实话，真的撑不下去。下午的时候我就离职跑路。但我跑路前，那帮男的在机器前依然很有激情。

怎么评价我这次当 “男人” 的体验呢… 说实在的，现在我回想起来还是很怕。我想不到底层男性的工作会这么辛苦，钱会这么难赚。尽管我去的时候就有心理准备。但我依然想象不到长年累月体力工作者是怎么坚持下来的。

现在回想起女拳头子比划着手指说：努力需要多大的劲啊… 我真的希望她能去工厂体验一下一天底层男性的生活。那种恶劣的小工厂住宿条件，一加班就十三四个小时的工作，没有空调，只有工业电扇的工作环境… 但凡体验过一天，她都真说不出 “努力需要多大的劲” 这种话

这次之后我对男性的改观比之前要大。此前我承认男人不易，现在实打实让我当了下 “男人”，去工厂工作，吃着包菜炒包菜配米饭。我得说，我一周都坚持不下去…

而现在很多网上在嘲讽国男的，还有那些把自己爹叫做生物爹的。可能她的爸爸、哥哥、兄弟就在这样的环境里上班。为多赚一点钱每天不惜加班四五个小时，回家还因为态度冷漠、说话生硬、拿不出足够的钱来被挂上 xhs 嘲讽无能。一想到这些，一想到同为女性，我身边还有那些不知道来钱辛苦的姊妹嘲讽她的兄弟就觉得羞愧难当。

唉，都互相体谅吧… 谁对谁也不是应该的。

item.title: 法国中学生抗议升级纵火案增加 警察逮捕5000人
item.description:
来源: 
新唐人

法国的学生抗议，今天也再次升级了。警方最新统计显示，参与抗议的学校已经达到了1200所，累计逮捕人数高达5000人，比前一天的1027所暴增将近20%，逮捕人数也增加了一倍多。

那要是从现场情况来看，昨天晚上10点多，梅斯市有一所初中学校，名字叫做“弗朗索瓦·拉伯雷”，发生了重大火灾，整个学校陷入一片火海，除了主教学楼之前，全都被烧了。

从现场画面可以看到，火势是相当大了。当地消防部门甚至出动了20辆消防、救援车，50名消防员都参与了灭火行动。现场还有3辆汽车被烧毁。

有民众看到事发当时，好几个人一起逃离了现场。特别是最近在全国爆发了学生抗议，我们之前节目也说过，出现了校园设施被纵火的情况，比如南特的“纳尔逊·曼德拉”高中、还有马赛的“维克多·雨果”，以及“圣埃克絮-佩里”高中。所以有人怀疑这是抗议团体故意纵火，不敢检方虽然没有确认、但也并没排除这个可能性。

那这些抗议群体除了继续到处纵火之外，今天更多的是对民众进行人身攻击。有一群抗议学生在天桥上扔重物、试图砸毁下面通过的车辆；还有一名抗议男子拿着灭火器对着人群喷射；还有人拿瓶子砸警察的头、甚至是直接攻击警察。最可怕的是，有人竟然对着一名女性的脸喷火。

那因为这些画面都太过暴力，我们是没办法在节目里展示的。但可以想像啊，现场有多么混乱、可怕。不过现在随着抗议升级，反对抗议的民众也出现了。

比如说在卡昂这个地方，有一位看起来上了年纪的女士，从阳台上拿着手枪就出来了，朝着楼下的抗议人群挥舞；还有个男子是在和抗议学生抢夺自己的垃圾桶。那其实是在抗议期间，有很多人都把垃圾桶搬到了学校门口当路障，或者就直接点燃了。

但是这其中最抢眼的，还是一些学生的家长。他们在抗议人群中抓着自己的孩子就往外拖，甚至还有父母一路狂追还在抗议的孩子。

可以看到画面中，这对父母是一边怒斥着孩子，一边抓着衣领就给拖回去了。或许对于这些年轻人来说，还真是需要一点严格的管束啊。

不过今天还出现了一个令人震惊的画面，就是警察像以前一样拿着警棍和盾牌驱逐抗议人群的时候，人群并没有散开，而是站在原地，甚至对着警察一阵唏嘘，把警察逼得的节节后退。

我们昨天的节目中其实也讲过，就是法国的法律是怎么规定的呢，只要你在被警察驱逐之后马上离开，就不能定罪。但是现在是什么情况呢？连警察都驱散不了这些抗议人群了，反而是警察自己被逼退，那难道说这些人就不怕被抓吗？

其中有一些自称是“安提法”、也就是“反法西斯运动”的人就宣称什么呢，说“如果警察冲向你的时候你不跑，他们就会撤退。”听起来就像是在鼓动抗议人民和警察去对抗，然后利用人数优势试图压制警察。那我们知道安提法这些人是已经被美国政府认定为恐怖组织的，那么接下来，法国抗议到底会如何发展，新闻第一线也会为您持续追踪。

item.title: 2 people killed and 35 injured at neighborhood block party shooting in southern Georgia
item.description:
VIENNA, Ga. (AP) — Law enforcement officials are still working to determine just what happened when a chaotic homecoming party spanning a four-block radius of a southern Georgia town erupted in gunfire early Sunday, leaving two people dead and nearly three dozen others injured.

Dooly County Sheriff Craig Peavy identified the two people killed as 21-year-old Jaquevion Jackson of Cordele and 23-year-old Macaleb Jackson of Hawkinsville, Georgia.

Some of the three dozen injured had gunshot wounds, Georgia Bureau of Investigation Chris Hosey said Sunday evening, but he could not provide a number.

“We’re still trying to work through that,” Hosey said during a news conference Sunday evening.

No arrests had been reported hours later, and authorities gave no possible motive for the gunfire.

The injured ranged in age from 14 to 51, and they were taken to several regional hospitals, Peavy said. Some were in critical condition Sunday evening and others were stable, he said.

More than 1,000 people attended the party

More than 1,000 people had gathered at the site, and more than 50 shots were fired in at least two locations about a block apart in Vienna, Peavy told WMAZ-TV. Vienna is a small, rural community about 130 miles (about 210 kilometers) south of Atlanta.

Deputies were near the scene when the shooting began, Peavy said, and after they arrived more gunfire erupted about a block away.

“We don’t know if it’s coming at us or someone else,” he said. “You just have to keep doing what you’re doing and hope you don’t get hit by gunfire.”

The incident took place over homecoming weekend for Dooly County High School.

One woman recalled rapid-fire shots and people running

Ashley Gee, 30, who lives in nearby Turner County and came to Vienna for the party, described to the Atlanta Journal-Constitution a constant barrage of gunfire, imitating the sound of rapid-fire shots.

“Like a machine gun,” she said. “One person ran, and everybody started running.”

The AJC said the party drew in people from other surrounding counties in south Georgia following a local high school football team’s victory at a homecoming game Friday night.

The shooting was not at a school-sponsored event, said Sherrod Willaford, superintendent of the Dooly County School System.

“We recognize that its impact may reach many of our students, families, and staff,” he said in a statement. Schools will open Monday, he said, but additional safety measures have been put in place. He did not specify what they are.

Peavy said the festivities began Friday night, and that it had “gone well” with “respect from the community” that evening as deputies patrolled the event.

Sheriff says deputies were on hand as shots were still being fired

But the party Saturday night was a “different story,” he said.

“We’re still working through the investigation to see what went wrong. But at large parties with people from different places, not just your locals, sometimes problems come,” he said.

"Our deputies were just about on the scene when it happened. They were at the end of each, most directions of where the block party was being held. But it was so many people. And it was just hard to figure out what was going on,” he said.

Peavy said the shooting was “a learning experience,” for his law enforcement team.

“There's just hardly no way to know how to operate when something like that happens on the scene," he said. He later continued, “We thought we'd been involved with a lot of stuff. But sometimes it surprises, and it was overwhelming.”

Vienna is about a 50-mile (80-kilometer) drive south on the Interstate 75 corridor from the central Georgia city of Macon, where authorities say 12 teens were wounded by gunfire during a confrontation between people at a birthday party the previous weekend a city park.

Deputies in Vienna found two people dead at the scene and multiple others who had been shot, officials said. Police also did not specify how many of the injured had been shot. The victims were taken to several hospitals for treatment, the GBI said.

Dooly County Coroner Brett Walls said the two men were pronounced dead at the scene with fatal gunshot wounds. He said multiple other people were also shot, calling the scene “horrific.”

Walls told the AJC that multiple people were struck by bullets and roughly a dozen others were hurt while trying to flee.

“This doesn’t — it’s not supposed to — happen in a small town like that. It’s something you hear on the news in bigger cities,” Walls told the newspaper, adding hospitals were flooded with the injured. “And even in bigger cities, you don’t hear that kind of a number.”

Investigators are seeking suspects and a motive

Authorities have not said whether any suspects are in custody or being sought. No motive has been given for the shooting.

Vienna Mayor Eddie Daniels said the shooting was about a block from his house and he “saw a lot of blue lights.” Daniels said he hadn’t spoken with law enforcement officials yet and had no details about what had happened.

Daniels said the city hadn’t issued any kind of permit for the block party and he didn’t know if it was a homecoming party.

Georgia Bureau of Investigation spokesperson Lydia Bullard declined to answer questions about the shooting, saying it was an ongoing investigation.

___

Associated Press reporters Rebecca Boone in Boise, Idaho, and Anthony Izaguirre in New York contributed to this report. Bauer reported from Madison, Wisconsin.

This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/2-shot-dead-dozens-injured-155033581.html

item.title: 严于律己，内找原因
item.description:
来源: 
正见网

一、严于律己，内找原因

有一天，鲁国国君问柳下惠：“我很想讨伐齐国，你认为怎么样？”柳下惠讲：“现在哪有这个必要呢？”

柳下惠回到家里以后，面带忧色，自言自语的说：“古圣有言：讨伐别国这样之事，莫向仁德者去询问。君主今天，为什么却把讨伐齐国的事，问到我的头上？可见我尚有仁德欠佳之处！”

齐国有个女子，来到了晏婴的门前。晏子见到了她，转身回到屋里，他虔心自省的问自己说：“我有淫欲的思想表现吗？为什么有女子奔到我这儿来？”

所以，有行贿的人拿着礼品、钱财上门，一定是因为主人有收贿之心；有小人在主公的身旁，一定是主人有了喜欢阿谀奉承的倾向。因此，有德行、有修养的人，体察自己要严，克制私欲要精心细致。要严于律己，内找原因！

二、学吉了之忠，用以报国……

有一个夷人，从中国买了一只秦吉了（一种鸟雀名）回到自己的国中。秦吉了忽然开口讲话，说：“我是汉鸟，不愿生活在你们的国家！”说完，就绝食饿死了。

明朝大历年间，有几百个猴子，聚集在一片枯树林中。村子里的人群，准备砍树，并且要杀死这一群猴子。这时一个老猴，忽然跳到邻近的一户人的房中，纵火烧屋。

村里的人们，便争相去救火。群猴就乘机从枯树上跑下来，逃走了。

希望人们：学吉了的忠诚，用以报效国家；效老猴的智慧，用以保全同类。

三、皇上的拐杖

宋寿皇在宫中时，常携带一个漆过的拄杖，表情十分庄重严肃，宦官和宫女们，平时都不敢正眼看他。

有一次，这位皇上游览后苑，忘了带拄杖，就命小黄门官回去取来。两个黄门官，使出了吃奶的劲，才把拄杖抬来。

原来，这根拄杖，是精铁铸成的。皇上有安定中原之志，所以，在私下里勤苦煆炼如此。

（以上均据郑瑄《昨非庵日纂》）

2010年11月27日

item.title: 文革中的一次抄家
item.description:
来源: 
来稿

1967年7月26日，父亲李世隆正在接受批斗，家里只有母亲和我们四个孩子，最小的弟弟才两岁。

那天，几个佩戴红袖章的造反派突然闯进家门，声称奉命对“走资派李世隆”实行抄家。母亲质问他们凭什么抄一个革命干部的家，对方却说现在是“造反有理”，随即开始翻箱倒柜。

母亲的小牛皮箱首先被打开。里面有她多年积攒的首饰、现金、公债、银行存单、全国粮票，还有几张留作纪念的第一套人民币。造反派不由分说，全部收走。母亲坚持要求登记财物，最后双方分别记录了收缴物品的名称和数量，并签字确认。

父亲的书房也被翻得乱七八糟。他珍藏的《史记》《资治通鉴》等线装古籍，被当作“封建糟粕”收走。军事教材、备课笔记和《干部必读》等书籍被扔在地上，任人踩踏。

有人从厨房的炉灰坑里搜出一个油布包，里面是父亲的工作笔记，记录着他转业以及负责钢厂基建工作的经历。造反派如获至宝，将笔记本也带走了。

抄家持续了两个小时。临走时，他们又看上了父亲珍爱的英国三枪牌自行车。那是父亲当年托人从上海买来的，平时擦得一尘不染。造反派说“走资派不配骑这么好的车”，便骑走了。

从此，家里的生活更加艰难。父母的工资被扣发，我们每人每月只有8元生活费。为了节省燃料开支，我到江边捡拾洪水冲下来的木柴，还到工厂锅炉炉渣里捡炭。

一个月后，父亲被关进“牛棚”。造反派不准母亲与他见面，只允许我们几个孩子在星期天送饺子时探望。

父亲瘦了，两鬓也白了，却仍然安慰我：“没事，我们解放了全中国，还不能解放自己吗！爸爸会解放的。”

母亲把她唯一的一件旗袍改成了我的棉袄。多年以后，我仍然记得那件织锦缎棉袄贴在胸前的感觉。

1971年春天，父亲终于恢复工作，回到了家。

几天后，当年参与抄家的人又来了。这次，他们带回了部分收缴的财物，包括父亲的工作笔记、全国粮票、已经兑换成现金的公债和银行存单。

母亲清点后问起那些线装古籍、姥姥留给她的手镯、第一套人民币，还有父亲的自行车。

来人说，古籍已经被当作封建糟粕烧掉，其余东西也找不到了。

父亲劝母亲算了，但那些东西毕竟是我们家多年的积蓄和珍藏，尤其是姥姥留下的手镯，寄托着母亲对她的思念，哪里是说忘就能忘记的。

如今，母亲的小牛皮箱还放在哥哥家的衣柜顶上。那些失而复得的粮票、父亲的功勋章、奖章和肩章，依然保存在箱子里。父亲的工作笔记则一直由我珍藏。

只是母亲的手镯、第一套人民币、父亲收藏的线装古籍，以及那辆三枪牌自行车，再也没有回来。

几十年过去了，每当想起那次抄家，眼前仍会浮现母亲护着我们几个孩子、看着家中财物被一件件搬走的情景。

那些失去的东西，有些已经无法估价，有些则永远无法弥补。

它们留在了1967年的那个夏天，也留在了我们一家人的记忆里。

资料来源：李长庆《抄家》，原载“新三届”。

item.title: 监狱琐记66：1963年—1966年的大陆高校清理“反动学生”事件
item.description:
来源: 
监狱琐记

建国以来，改革开放以前“反动学生”这个词虽也常见于教育系统的内部通报，但真正作为政治帽子、作为正式处分大学生一个案由，只实行于1963年到1966年清理反动学生运动中。到了1966年有些特殊，如果是年初划的、并送劳改了，也就是“反动学生”了；如果拖到“文革”起来了，到了7月，毛主席下令不许“整学生”，说“凡是镇压学生运动的人都没有好下场”，并指出北洋军阀镇压、蒋介石镇压学生运动都没有好下场。于是这批“反动学生”也就一风吹了，而此前的“反动学生”依然在劳改场劳动改造，直至1969年1月24日起，被各校陆续派员召回为止，嗣后，有的随1966年—1968年三届毕业学生分配；有的延宕至1970年随1969届学生一起分配工作或劳动；有的不幸，再次戴上帽子驱逐回原籍农村监督劳动（如人民大学的“反动学生”）。

一、缘起

1957年反右之后，为了证明这次“反击资产阶级右派分子猖狂进攻”的政治决策的正确伟大，必然要掀起一个社会主义的建设高潮，形象些说就是“三面红旗”上马。建设的目的意在推动经济增长，提升国力，“超英赶美”，然而推动经济建设的手段仍是像战争时期“群众运动”和“阶级斗争”并用。群众运动中不积极者或有怨气者（过大的劳动强度和无报酬的强迫劳动）就被视为阶级敌人的破坏行为。轻者要被群众“辩论”（批斗的另一种表达），重者也有被戴上政治帽子或法办的。通过三年“大干快上”随之而来的是“三年困难时期”，全国普遍没饭吃了。饥饿是最教育人的，“假大空”、官话、套话是解决不了肚子问题的。

本来宣称要实现人类最美好的“共产主义天堂”，反而滑向了死亡和饥饿的地狱。反差极大，震撼极深。此时本应出现“其咎在谁”的历史追问，古今中外，没有例外。然而在中国出现了例外，由于信息封闭和舆论控制，这种追问并未形成。困居城市的人们，因为情况稍好，不知农村实际情况；困居农村者，缺少表达能力，许多也是“死者长已矣”。但封闭不可能是铁板一块，城乡沟通渠道，没有因为城乡二元的户口制度而彻底隔绝，例如，从农村进城学习的学生、城乡之间有亲戚关系往来者都会把真实消息传入城市，给人们以震撼。其中受冲击最大的当属没有政治经验、但良知尚未泯灭的学生，最美的理想和最糟糕的现实之间形成巨大的反差，这是为什么？

其次是“反修运动”，这要求学生思想来个180度的转弯。自1930年代以来，左派文化界一直宣传苏联是何等的美好，简直就是人间天堂。五六十年代的学生都是在俄苏文化哺育下成长起来的。那时提起“世界”就是苏联，提起奋斗目标就是苏联的今天是我们的明天；提起真善美，就是俄苏文化中的文学艺术……许多中学生都有固定的苏联学生作为笔友。1959年以前，谁要是对俄苏有句负面评论，最轻也要划右派、受批判。怎么能想象突然有一天，苏联变修，成为比帝国主义还要坏的“社会帝国主义”，这不是与蒋介石所说“赤色帝国主义对中国威胁更大”出于一辙吗？

这是政治和社会背景对青年学生思想的冲击。另外1960年末至1962年下半年，因为经济困难，政治控制相对缓和，文化上也相对开放，上演了一些“大、洋、古”作品，开放了一些欧美（拉丁美洲）电影，这些作品中的人道主义对青年有所影响，特别是文科学生。

由于吃不饱，高校也不搞运动了，斗争也少了。校方为了安定同学的思想情绪，强调“劳逸结合”“保持热量”，倡导多睡觉、少读书。这样，自1957年以来那种人人自危氛围淡漠了，出现了后来校方所说的“自由化倾向”（他们不懂得人本来就应该这样生活），有的高校还发生了“选举问题”（同学们不愿意选举由系总支安排的人做班干部）。

1962年下半年，经济好转，北戴河会议上毛泽东强调“千万不要忘记阶级与阶级斗争”，后来农村的“四清”城市的“五反”都是贯彻这一方针的表现，于是，也开始关注学生领域的问题。

整“反动学生”始于1963年暑假的北京高校毕业生毕业鉴定时。据1963年河北北京师院数学系毕业生朱志曾先生回忆说，毕业前，学校要求每个人都写自我鉴定（政治性的），然后集体讨论通过才能毕业。在写鉴定之前，校方传达了北京市委大学工作部和北京高教局的文件。文件说在北京高教领域存在着尖锐的阶级斗争，毕业生中就有阶级敌人，并公布了一些案例。有北大的“反动小集团”案，科技大的“叛国投敌”案等，给人印象最深的是北京地质学院尚育森投书中央广播电台“驳斥国际共产主义运动总路线”案。1963年6月14日，《关于国际共产主义运动总路线的建议》（简称“(25)条”）发表，广播电台日夜广播，声势很大，北京地质学院物理勘探专业的尚育森是个山东汉子，对“25条”有异议，马上给中央台写了一封据说有7000字的信，要求在反修防修问题上公开辩论，结果被定为北京的第一个“反动学生”。

此事被北京市委书记彭真报告给了毛泽东，1963年7月下发了《中共中央、国务院关于高等学校应届毕业生中政治上反动的学生处理通知》（见国家教育委员会编：《高等学校学籍管理文件汇编：1950—1987》）。毛泽东的批示，指出这类现象所在多有，这是一批极右分子。文件说“据北京市反映，今年高等学校应届毕业生中，有极少数政治上反动的学生……其对我的猖狂进攻的程度已经相当甚至超过反右斗争中的极右分子”，“北京市的高等院校有这样的情况，全国高等院校，也必然同样有这种情况。对这一小撮政治反动的学生，必须抓紧时机，通过揭露与批判，对他们进行严肃认真的处理”。根据这个文件的精神，教育部经国务院文教办批准制定了《关于高等学校应届毕业生中政治上反动的学生在劳动教养或劳动考察期间的试行管理办法》。于是从1963年暑期前起，在全国大专院校中清理“反动学生”。第一批“反动学生”被清理出来了，计有尚育森、朱志曾、李明昌（河北北京师院）以及北大的吴启元、伉铁保、科技大的马家骅等。于1964年送往红星农场劳动改造。

选自王学泰著《监狱琐记》，生活·读书·新知三联书店，2013年10月

item.title: Trump adviser says Americans' spending tells a different story than economic polls
item.description:
National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett insisted to CNN's "State of the Union" on Sunday that he doesn't believe in recent polls that show the public's negative feelings about the economy.

"Ahead of an election cycle, the fact that there's, you know, possibly partisan pollsters telling us that the people are really, really depressed, it's a classic Democrat move, and I just don't buy it," Hassett said.

"Because if it were true, if the polls were any value for thinking about what's going on with consumers, then we should look at the consumption data and say, Jeez, yeah, that's right. People aren't spending. But, in fact, the retailers are doing well."

Hassett added that he's often put in a double bind by the type of questions asked by opponents of the Trump administration.

"If I say, 'Oh, people are wrong, the economy's great,' then it looks like I'm insensitive. And if I then go into why the economy is great, then it looks like I'm insensitive," he said. "And so let's just unpack it and start with, well, people are saying that the economy's not great.

"It's true that the polls, which have gotten the president's success wrong every time, have been saying that people are looking a little bit depressed about the economy. But if you look at their actions, the actions speak way louder than words."

Hassett explained that "what we know from the economic literature is that, if people are worried about whether they're going to lose their job, if they're worried about whether they're going to get a pay cut, then they start reducing their consumption and increasing their savings. It's called the buffer-stock theory of savings.

"And so what we see right now is that people are really, really optimistic about the future, about their future incomes, because they're spending really, really at record levels. They're defaulting at their credit card debt at really, really low levels.

Hassett emphasized that "the consumer information data came out [this past week] that showed that consumption was up year over year at the highest rate in years. We have got GDP now for the third quarter running 4 to 5%."

He insisted that people are saying, they are confident with their jobs, and that they remained confident GDP growth was coming.

Hassett added, "And the polls are different from that. And so then the question is, Are the people wrong or the pollsters wrong? And I would say the pollsters are wrong."

item.title: 菲律宾指责中国海警在中业岛附近阻挠其执法行动
item.description:
来源: 
美国之音

菲律宾海岸警卫队星期日(10月4日)表示，中国船只阻挠了菲方针对一艘涉嫌在南中国海中业岛(菲律宾称帕加萨岛)附近进行炸鱼作业的外国渔船所开展的执法行动。

菲方形容中国海军直升机的出现是一种“不必要的恐吓行为”。这是马尼拉与北京之间近期一系列海上对峙事件中的最新一起。

此次行动涉及菲律宾海岸警卫队、海军及国家警察海事小组的人员，其行动针对在中业岛以西约三海里处有外国渔船涉嫌炸鱼的活动。

菲律宾海岸警卫队称，两艘中国海警船鸣响汽笛，通过无线电向菲方发出警告，随后对菲方船只进行跟踪和阻拦。一架中国人民解放军海军直升机也在菲方人员上空盘旋了四次。

菲方人员曾命令该外国渔船停船并多次通过无线电进行呼叫，但该船无视指令，朝西南方向驶向渚碧礁(Subi Reef，菲律宾称三莫拉礁)，这是中国在南沙群岛为支持其主权主张而建造的七个人工岛礁之一。

出于安全考虑，菲方终止了追逐并返回中业岛。

菲海岸警卫队表示，中国海警在中业岛领海内“没有执法权”，并称其行动“助长了涉嫌违规者的逃脱”。菲方还驳斥了中方关于其船只被驱逐出该区域的任何说法。

中业岛面积约0.4平方公里，四周环绕珊瑚礁，是菲律宾在南沙群岛控制的九个岛礁中最大且最具战略价值的一个，距离菲律宾本土450公里。

此外，菲军方表示，星期六在有争议的黄岩岛(Scarborough Shoal)上空，一架中国歼-16战斗机多次接近并贴近一架菲律宾巡逻机进行机动飞行，构成了航空安全风险。 菲律宾武装部队表示，此次事件是针对正在执行合法任务的菲律宾船只和飞机的反复进行的“不安全及胁迫性行为”的一部分。

中国驻马尼拉大使馆未立即回应路透社就周末发生的事件置评的请求。

南中国海是连接东亚、东南亚、中东、非洲与欧洲的重要航运通道，是全球约三分之一海上贸易的必经之路。中国和菲律宾经常在南中国海争议水域发生激烈的对峙和对抗。

中国声称拥有几乎整个南中国海的主权，但是2016年海牙国际仲裁法院作出裁决，驳回北京基于历史权利的南中国海9段线主张。但是北京既不参与仲裁，也拒不接受仲裁结果。

美国对南中国海岛礁主权归属不持立场，但坚持维护航行和飞越自由，并明确表示各方海洋权利主张须符合国际法。美国与菲律宾于1951年签署了《共同防御条约》。

关键词: 
菲律宾
中国海警
中业岛
中国渔船
南中国海

item.title: Sam Altman says the world should accept 'some bad things' for AI's benefits
item.description:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said there remains a fundamental difference in worldview between his company and rival Anthropic on artificial intelligence regulation, arguing in an exclusive interview with Decoded by POLITICO that the technology’s benefits justify accepting some risks — and that AI should remain broadly accessible to the public.

“I think there's a lot of daylight,” Altman told Decoded co-author and POLITICO senior tech reporter Brendan Bordelon. Asked specifically where he diverges from Anthropic and its CEO Dario Amodei, Altman said, “we believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology and people having the agency.”

Anthropic has long been viewed as the strongest proponent of AI regulations within the industry, a stance that until recently was at odds with the lighter-touch approach favored by OpenAI. But the policy differences between the two leading AI firms have narrowed in recent months, with OpenAI backing tougher rules as it grapples with high-profile hacking incidents and rogue behavior by its models.

Altman agreed with Amodei’s call last month to slow the development of the most advanced AI models. His company has followed Anthropic in endorsing new state laws that impose stricter safety requirements than what the maker of ChatGPT had previously supported — a subtle shift from its prior state strategy. And OpenAI lobbyists recently endorsed a bipartisan House proposal that would require top AI companies to embed outside safety evaluators.

Despite the convergence, Altman tried to distinguish his firm’s regulatory stance from Anthropic’s, referencing a criticism about regulatory capture that tech advisers close to President Donald Trump have applied to Anthropic.

“I disagree, but I understand the perspective of people who are like, ‘This technology is going to get so powerful, and it’s so dangerous, that a single lab in San Francisco should have it and make sure nothing bad happens, and kind of figure out how to dole out the benefits,’” said Altman. He called it “a completely unacceptable trade-off” that runs counter to the “lighter-touch regulatory stance” backed by OpenAI.

“I wouldn't take a trade of saying, ‘We'll make sure there's no major hacks, there's no misuse of this technology, there's zero scams, there's zero all the other bad things that will happen,’” said Altman. “Because I think people will do tremendously — orders of magnitude more — good stuff than bad stuff.”

The OpenAI CEO later added that he does not accept “the really catastrophic risks,” including the potential for “a serious loss of control to AI.”

Asked to respond, an Anthropic spokesperson said that its “regulatory proposals apply only to frontier models.” The company also referred to an August social media exchange that Amodei had with an investment manager, addressing criticisms around regulatory capture and impacts on smaller companies.

“Anthropic has always made its policy proposals very carefully,” Amodei said at the time. “We try very hard to make proposals that disadvantage (slow down) frontier AI companies while *advantaging* smaller competitors.”

The Altman interview, appearing in Monday’s debut edition of Decoded and its accompanying daily podcast, also delved into Trump’s new AI accord with top tech firms and his attempted “superintelligence” rebrand; the rash of autonomous hacking incidents carried out by OpenAI models and whether the company should face legal liability; Altman’s thoughts on the AI industry money swamping U.S. politics; the influence of so-called effective altruists inside OpenAI; and his views on key political power players including French President Emmanuel Macron and California Gov. Gavin Newsom.

Decoded by POLITICO — produced by Brendan, Christine Mui, Calder McHugh and Sam Sutton — draws on the reporting of some 50 POLITICO journalists around the world to cover not just where tech is going, but the personalities, policy fights and political battles taking it there. Subscribe to the newsletter and to the podcast.

This article originally appeared on Politico at https://www.politico.com/news/2026/10/04/sam-altman-decoded-interview-ai-01106217

item.title: 德国总理默茨突访基辅之际，俄罗斯再次空袭乌克兰首都
item.description:
来源: 
美国之音

俄罗斯星期天(10月4日)再次对包括首都基辅在内的乌克兰多地发动新的袭击，基辅又一座主要桥梁成为俄军的攻击目标。俄军新一轮针对基辅的袭击发生时，德国总理弗里德里希·默茨(Friedrich Merz)刚刚抵达乌克兰首都进行一次未曾预告的突然访问。

根据法新社报道，整个星期天上午，基辅各地的防空警报声此起彼伏。当乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基(Volodymyr Zelensky)在基辅的国家科学院会晤默茨时，室外的警报声也一再响起。国家科学院本身上周一也曾遭到俄罗斯攻击型无人机的袭击。

泽连斯基在会晤时告诉默茨，基辅市民因俄军持续不断的袭击而饱受“恐怖日夜”的煎熬。他称俄罗斯为“彻头彻尾的野蛮人”。

“在这个地方，我们可以看到这场战争是多么毫无意义，”默茨在会谈中表示。“针对乌克兰平民的野蛮袭击必须停止。这里每天都在发生战争罪行。”

基辅市长维塔利·克利奇科(Vitalii Klitschko)表示，在过去四天里，横跨第聂伯河并连接基辅东部和西部的多座桥梁屡遭俄军袭击。俄军星期六和星期天连续两天袭击损坏了“北桥”(Northern Bridge)的路面，导致城市交通中断并引发漫长的道路拥堵。而“南桥”则在稍早连续遭到多次打击。

克利奇科指出，尽管基辅在近五年的俄乌冲突中基本未受前线战火的蹂躏，但鉴于俄军袭击次数激增，该市现在必须进入战时状态。

连日来，俄军一连串不分昼夜的袭击击中了居民区、加油站、学校以及铁路和通信基础设施。而几乎不间断的防空警报不仅扰乱了日常生活，更让民众时刻处于高度紧张和不安之中。

默茨在抵达基辅时表示，乌克兰“在未来几周内需要我们全力支持”。

“如果不能阻止俄罗斯，它的战争机器迟早会把矛头指向我们，”默茨又说。

泽连斯基星期六在接受路透社专访时表示，乌克兰情报部门获取的文件显示，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京(Vladimir Putin)发布了一项“新指令”，允许俄军在即将到来的冬季对乌克兰平民目标发动更大规模的打击。

“我们看到了相关文件，也知道这些文件允许他们攻击基础设施、后勤设施、道路、学校和医院，以此施压迫使民众离开首都及其他城市，”泽连斯基说。他指出，尽管俄军在战场上不断失利并遭受惨重伤亡，但普京此举意在展示强硬姿态。

针对莫斯科战术的转变，泽连斯基誓言要加强对俄罗斯能源设施的打击以示报复，但强调不会无差别地以俄罗斯平民为目标。

“我们必须采取一切可能的手段进行回击。既然他们攻击我们的能源设施，我们也必须回击他们的能源设施。首要目标是炼油厂--因为那是他们为这场战争筹集资金的来源，”泽连斯基说。

“当然，我们绝不会像他们那样，去攻击任何民用目标。”

泽连斯基星期六表示，作为对俄罗斯袭击民用目标的回应，乌克兰动用远程导弹打击了俄罗斯萨马拉地区的一处设施，以及布良斯克地区的“伊斯坎德尔”(Iskander)导弹系统。

美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)连续几个星期一直敦促乌克兰和俄罗斯停止袭击对方的能源设施，以帮助降低因美国和伊朗的冲突而引发的高油价。尽管泽连斯基表示愿意与俄尝试达成能源设施停火，但莫斯科对特朗普的呼吁似乎并没有什么回应。

乌克兰一直希望能获得更多西方军事支持和援助，包括能够击落俄罗斯新型高速喷气式无人机的先进拦截武器。

泽连斯基星期天表示乌克兰将达成“重要协议”。而法新社援引柏林政府消息人士的话说，德乌双方预计将敲定一项价值超过10亿美元的新军事援助计划。

德国消息人士表示，该计划包括用于帮助乌克兰打击俄罗斯发射阵地的作战无人机和卫星技术，以及联合生产反喷气式无人机的项目。

“这项援助填补了乌克兰防空系统当前最严重的缺口，预计将产生迅速而切实的成效，” 法新社援引一位不具名消息人士的话说。

由于欧洲日益担忧自己可能成为俄罗斯的下一个攻击目标，默茨日前呼吁北约和欧洲保持团结以应对俄罗斯。他同时也呼吁德国国内团结一致，因为德国极右翼且亲俄的反对党“德国选择党”(AfD)势力正日益壮大。

据德国政府消息人士透露，默茨此次突访基辅，有可能宣布向乌克兰提供约3.5亿欧元的援助，用于购置发电机和变电站设备以及修复电网。

item.title: 阿联酋曾与以色列分享迪拜航空航班详细信息，但以方并未对任何乘客或机组人员提出安全疑虑
item.description:
来源: 
美国之音

阿拉伯联合酋长国迪拜航空(FlyDubai)一架飞往以色列的班机险遭副驾驶劫持的空中惊魂事件持续引起地区以及全球的高度关注。

当地一些官员星期天(10月4日)透露，在涉事航班起飞前，阿联酋当局已经向航班目的地的以色列政府提供了乘客和机组人员的名单，其中还包括飞行员的姓名和国籍资料。这些新披露的信息引起人们对涉案副驾驶如何逃过安全审查的新疑问。

上周三，一架载有182名乘客和机组人员的迪拜航空 FZ1073航班正从迪拜飞往以色列特拉维夫，途中副驾驶使用驾驶舱内的应急斧砍伤了印度籍机长斯米特·马查尔(Smit Machchhar)，并试图控制飞机。机长负伤后打开驾驶舱门寻求帮助。

袭击发生后，飞机曾一度在30秒之内急剧下坠约5,180米，随后在乘客和机组人员制服袭击者后，由同机的一名迪拜航空备用飞行员重新控制了飞机。

该航班随即改变航向，被迫在沙特阿拉伯西北部塔布克(Tabuk)的苏丹本·阿卜杜勒-阿齐兹亲王国际机场(Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz International Airport)紧急降落。

涉案副驾驶已被确认为阿曼籍公民哈马姆·哈马米(Hammam al-Hammami)。此人被沙特当局逮捕，并移交给负责此次调查的阿联酋。

随着调查的展开，有关该事件的初步细节凸显出一些重大的安全疏漏。

哈马米曾因其极端主义观点在其本国阿曼遭禁飞。令人特别疑惑不解的是一名来自与以色列没有外交关系的阿拉伯国家的公民、一名因极端主义思维而在本国遭禁飞的飞行员，为何获准驾驶满载以色列乘客的航班飞往特拉维夫？

美联社援引地区官员的话说，阿联酋当局已分享了有关乘客和机组人员的信息，其中包括他们的国籍。这些不具名官员表示，以色列并未对任何乘客或机组人员提出安全疑虑或发出警示。

根据美联社的报道，以色列国内安全机构“辛贝特”(Shin Bet)表示，交通部负责审查来自外国航班的乘客名单。交通部长米里·雷格夫(Miri Regev)告诉以色列公共广播公司(Kan)，飞行安全由安全机构负责，而她的部门并未收到乘客名单或任何相关警告。

分享名单是航空业的标准程序。但以色列交通部航空安全负责人德维尔·鲁本斯坦(Dvir Rubenstien)告诉陆军电台，该部依赖当地的安全检查，既无手段也无能力对每一趟航班上的每一位乘客进行检查。

以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡(Benjamin Netanyahu)上周四表示，以色列与外国航空公司长期以来签有协议，禁止那些来自与以色列无外交关系国家的飞行员飞往该国。

内塔尼亚胡上周五还表示，以色列正在调查涉事副驾驶是否受他人指使行事，并警告称任何涉案人员都将付出“沉重代价”。

由于以色列月底将面临大选，此次空中恐怖袭击未遂事件已经很快从安全议题蔓延至政治口水战。一些反对派候选人似乎抓住飞安疏漏开始做政治文章，以凸显内塔尼亚胡及其支持者的“失职”。交通部长雷格夫是内塔尼亚胡所属利库德集团(Likud party)的成员，也是其坚定支持者。

“这正是系统崩溃的写照：一位对领空安全完全撒手不管的交通部长，以及一位置国家安全于不顾的总理,”美联社援引反对派“民主党”(Democrats party)领导人亚伊尔·戈兰(Yair Golan)在社交平台X上的贴文说。

与此同时，对涉案者哈马米的调查已经超越中东，延申至他曾经留学过的澳大利亚。

路透社援引两名获悉调查情况的消息人士的话说，哈马米曾在澳大利亚维多利亚州首府墨尔本的一所大学学习。当地媒体报道称，他就读于皇家墨尔本理工大学(RMIT)。但该校向路透社表示，对此事不予置评。

“由澳大利亚联邦警察(AFP)、维多利亚州警方和澳大利亚安全情报组织(ASIO)组成的维多利亚州联合反恐小组(VIC JCTT)证实，正在调查该男子与澳大利亚的关联。将在适当时候提供最新情况，”路透社援引澳大利亚联邦警察一位发言人的话说。

英国《金融时报》星期天援引两名知情人士的话报道说，哈马米在澳大利亚期间据称曾造访激进清真寺并浏览极端主义网站。

报道说，澳大利亚情报部门掌握着有关他个人的档案。

关键词: 
阿联酋
以色列
迪拜航班袭击事件
栏目: 
要闻

item.title: U.S. removes all bombers from British base targeted by a suspected terror plot
item.description:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The U.S. Air Force has brought home its bombers stationed at a U.S.-run military air base in England used to strike Iran following an investigation into a planned terror attack at the RAF Fairford base.

The bombers were redeployed to their home bases in the United States, according to a Pentagon official who was not authorized to discuss sensitive military movements and spoke Sunday on condition of anonymity.

Aviation watchers such as the Military Air Tracking Alliance have observed dozens of B-52 and B-1 bombers operating out of RAF Fairford since the opening days of the Iran war. Observers noticed a host of B-1 bombers fly out of the base on Sunday.

The move comes as President Donald Trump weighs options for his war on Iran — including new strikes — despite his initial promises to Americans that the campaign would last a matter of weeks.

“We have decisions that I’ll make about Iran. Iran’s been decimated. So the only question is — it’ll either be the easy way, or the hard way,” Trump told reporters on Saturday as he left the White House for a rally in Ohio.

A dual British-Iranian national was arrested in central London last week on suspicion of plotting a terror attack, following a security incident at RAF Fairford in late September. In total, six people have been taken into custody and then released on bail during the investigation.

British authorities have linked the incident to Tehran. Iran has denied involvement, but it has previously said it considers any base used to attack its territory a legitimate target.

U.K. officials say proxies linked to Iran have been behind a string of arson and other attacks in Britain and other countries, many of them targeting the Jewish community and intended to sow fear. They have previously warned that Tehran could expand its targets in the U.K. if conflicts in the Middle East continue.

RAF Fairford, located 100 miles (160 kilometers) west of London, has been used by American bombers during decades of conflicts in the Middle East.

The U.S. military still maintains a sizable presence in the Middle East. On Thursday, a U.S. official said the recently deployed USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier, as well as the USS Malkin Island amphibious readiness group — a group of ships that together carry over 7,000 sailors and 2,000 Marines — are heading for the region. The official said the move could result in three carriers in the region as early as the end of October.

___

AP writer Melissa Goldin contributed from New York.

This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/us/articles/us-air-force-removes-bombers-205946225.html

item.title: 主要石油出口国同意在11月保持产量稳定
item.description:
来源: 
美国之音

由石油输出国组织(OPEC)及其包括俄罗斯在内的七个主要石油出口国组成的OPEC+集团，星期日(10月4日)原则上同意维持11月的产量目标不变。

由于伊朗战事，海湾地区的OPEC+产油国目前的实际产量远低于既定目标；近几个月来，其出口量一直在正常水平的60%至80%之间波动。

业内人士指出，这场冲突还推迟了该组织的产能评估工作--这对确定成员国2027年的产量配额至关重要--因为冲突使得对未来生产潜力的预估变得充满不确定性。

经历了多年的减产后，OPEC+在2026年的大部分时间里一直在上调产量目标，但由于中东冲突，这些增产计划大多仅停留在纸面上。

OPEC数据显示，OPEC+七个核心成员国8月份的日产量为2500万桶，较7月份增加了63万桶，但仍比2月份战前水平低约500万桶。

这一被称为“OPEC+”的小组成员包括沙特阿拉伯、俄罗斯、伊拉克、科威特、哈萨克斯坦、阿尔及利亚和阿曼。它们将于11月1日再次开会，评估国际石油市场状况。

目前，基准布伦特原油价格已升至每桶100美元以上。

七国工业集团(G7)成员国星期五(10月2日)宣布计划协调投放一亿桶柴油和原油，以期应对高企的能源价格。七国集团在一份联合声明中说，这些投放将在四个月内陆续进行，首先在20天内“大量释放柴油”。

七国集团说，“面对石油市场前所未有的波动--价格飙升威胁着经济稳定和我们的公民福祉--我们已就采取果断协调的措施达成一致，以稳定当前的能源供应，保护家庭和企业免受价格冲击，并加强全球能源系统的长期韧性。”

美国总统唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)星期五在他的真相社交(Truth Social)平台上称赞了这一举措，他说：“欧洲刚刚同意释放其大量储备的柴油。这个过程将立即启动。感谢你对此事的关注！”

关键词: 
石油出口
栏目: 
要闻

item.title: 巴西总统大选首轮投票结束：卢拉与博索纳罗之子激烈角逐 选民屏息等待结果
item.description: 巴西总统选举首轮投票周日（10月4日）结束，选民正屏息焦急等待选举结果。左翼现任总统卢拉与保守派对手弗拉维奥·博索纳罗展开激烈角逐，在拉美经历一股右转浪潮之际，特朗普称“密切关注选举”。

item.description: 德国总理默茨周日（10月4日）抵达基辅，表达对乌克兰的支持，并承诺提供超过13亿欧元的新一轮援助。同一天，基辅一座桥梁再遭俄罗斯袭击。泽连斯基宣布，美国计划于10月底与俄罗斯和乌克兰代表举行三方会谈。印度外交部长苏杰生表示，印度寻求在俄乌之间发挥更大的斡旋作用，推动结束战争。

item.title: 菲律宾指责中国海警阻挠南海执法 称军机近距离接近巡逻机
item.description: 菲律宾海岸警卫队周日(10月4日）表示，中国船只在南海由菲律宾控制的中业岛附近，阻挠菲方对一艘涉嫌使用炸药捕鱼的外国渔船开展执法行动。菲律宾军方并称，一架中国歼-16战斗机在存在主权争议的黄岩岛上空，多次近距离接近一架菲律宾巡逻机，造成航空安全风险。这是马尼拉与北京近期一系列海上对峙中的最新一起事件。

item.title: Coast Guard suspends search for 6 medical jet passengers off Nantucket
item.description:
The U.S. Coast Guard on Sunday suspended the search for six people in a medical jet that went missing near Nantucket, Massachusetts, a day after debris from the plane was found.

Search and rescue crews operated for approximately 66 hours to locate four Canadians and two Bermudian nationals on the plane that was traveling to Boston from Bermuda early Saturday morning, according to the U.S. Coast Guard.

The Canadian-registered air ambulance jet had four crew members and two passengers aboard. Their next of kin have been notified, the Coast Guard said.

Earlier, the Coast Guard confirmed that a debris field belonging to the missing Gulfstream G-100 was found Saturday night. The search for the missing passengers continued overnight off the coast of Nantucket, according to the Coast Guard's Northeast District, and spanned 4,445 miles before it was suspended.

The Coast Guard outlined the extensive assets involved in the search, including an HC-144 Ocean Sentry airplane, an HC-130 Hercules airplane, an MH-60 Jayhawk helicopter, a 47-foot Motor Lifeboat and the FRC William Sparling, a Sentinel-class fast response cutter.

"Suspending a search is not an easy decision," Rear Adm. Matthew Lake, Commander of the Northeast District, said in a statement. "We express our deepest condolences to the families and loved ones affected by the tragedy and our gratitude for our partner agencies who helped support search efforts."

The plane took off from Bermuda's L.F. Wade International Airport at about 11:40 p.m. ET on Friday, according to data from FlightAware. It went missing after about 1 hour and 45 minutes in the air. FlightAware data show it quickly dropped from about 24,000 feet to 11,000 feet before losing contact. It had been set to land at Boston's Logan International Airport at about 1:30 a.m. local time.

The Federal Aviation Administration confirmed it had lost contact with the plane around 1 a.m. local time Saturday and issued a Search and Rescue Alert Notice for the Gulfstream.

Canada's foreign policy department said it was "deeply concerned by the disappearance" of the plane in a statement Sunday.

"Our thoughts are with everyone on board and their loved ones," the statement said. "We thank the U.S. Coast Guard and all those involved in the search for their tireless efforts."

Officials haven't been able to identify the aircraft components found among the debris, said Kastriot Kastrati, coordinator of the Coast Guard's search and rescue mission, at a briefing Sunday.

"It's very difficult at this point to identify exactly what those components are," he said. "The debris that we have recovered, we've safeguarded and kept for future investigative efforts."

The National Transportation Safety Board told CBS News on Sunday that it is monitoring the situation.

"My thoughts are with everyone on board, as well as their families, loved ones and colleagues during this incredibly difficult time," Steve MacKinnon, Canada's minister of transport, said in a statement.

This article originally appeared on CBS News at https://www.cbsnews.com/news/medical-plane-missing-nantucket-six-on-board/

item.title: As he exits Senate, Tillis sounds alarm on 'outsized influence' of executive branch
item.description:
As Sen. Thom Tillis exits the Senate, he's blasting many of the advisers President Trump has surrounded himself with as "sycophants, and calling on his colleagues to stand up to executive power like the co-equal branch of government they are."

The 66-year-old senior senator from North Carolina unloads on what he calls the "WTF moments" of the second Trump Administration in a new book, "How to Lose Friends and Antagonize Presidents." Having served in the Senate during the Barack Obama, Joe Biden and both Trump presidencies, Tillis said he's increasingly worried about how the nation's system of checks and balances is being tested by the outsized influence of the executive branch.

"We will have a sort of dictator king if we're not careful," he said.

Make the Senate great again?

Every recent White House has been eager to govern by executive order, something that's been especially true during the current Trump administration, Tillis said. Presidents, he said, fail to understand that Congress is a coequal branch that should be treated as a peer, and that Congress needs to act as such.

"I would say the same thing for Democratic-controlled Senate under Biden and Obama," he said. "We always make the mistake when our guy's in office of conveying power to the White House. And I've had a real problem with that because it almost always comes back to bite you."

He writes in his book of the risks of authoritarianism. Tillis said there's been "constant escalation" across four administrations of presidents ignoring Congress. 

"I want checks and balances. I want all three branches to have their individual role and continue to check power as they have for 250 years," he said. "I think because we've been such a successful democracy for so long, it's hard for the American people to understand how quickly we can lose it all."

The Tillis tightrope act

Tillis was first elected to the Senate in the 2014 midterm elections, just before the rise of Mr. Trump and his Make America Great Again populist movement took over the Republican Party. He said he's the same kind of conservative now that he was back then: "pro-Second Amendment, pro-life, limited government, fiscal restraint."

"The only difference between me and a lotta people that call themselves true conservatives is I got a long list of things that were ratified and they don't," he said. 

The senator is now exiting Washington after a series of fights with the White House. The breaking point, he says, came in June 2025, after Tillis announced he would vote against Mr. Trump's One Big Beautiful Bill Act, arguing that it would push too many low-income North Carolinians off Medicaid. 

Mr. Trump responded by calling Tillis "a talker and complainer, not a doer," and threatening to back a primary challenger against Tillis. The senator decided he would retire instead of fighting for his seat. 

"I respect the president. I still feel like we have an odd relationship, where I've clearly made him angry," Tillis said recently. That was before details of his profanity-laced private texts with Trump about what prompted his retirement leaked, because Tillis included them as part of his upcoming book.  

Tillis said he is not done fighting, recently calling for Trump to fire Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

It should be noted that Tillis voted to confirm all of Mr. Trump's Cabinet nominees, including Hegseth.  But he now calls  that vote at the start of the second Trump Administration his "biggest regret." 

While Tillis said he is glad "the president went in" to Iran, he thinks "they got so caught up after the immense success of the first strike that Hegseth probably didn't listen to his best military advice and say, 'Now we should probably move to a different posture.'"

It's not the first time Tillis has gone after a member of Trump's cabinet. Last March at a senate hearing, he leveled a blistering critique of Department of Homeland Security Advisor Kristi Noem, calling out, among other things, the way she handled the deaths of Renee Good and Alex Pretti in Minneapolis.  that went viral, Tillis ripped into Noem. "I was thinking about her calling people that were shot, potentially domestic terrorists," he said. "That's proven not to be true."

Two days later, the president fired her.  

"I think Noem and Hegseth are probably the poster children for men and women who should never have the authority they've been granted," Tillis said. 

It's one example of the tightrope that Tillis has walked in the second Trump administration: saying how much he wants the president to succeed, while heaping blame on his advisers and subordinates. Besides Noem and Hegseth, Tillis s also highly critical of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and White House deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller, for "not looking around corners for" Mr. Trump.

Tillis' balancing act in Washington also extends to the events of Jan. 6, 2021. The senator is still angry about the attack on the Capitol, and threat to the peaceful transfer of power, calling what happened that day "despicable." Still, Tillis elected not to convict Mr. Trump after he left office during his second impeachment trial, criticizing the process as rushed and politicized.

"Cheapening the impeachment process to prevent somebody from running in the future, I just don't buy it," he said.

An "electoral bloodbath" in the midterms

Asked if he fears a Jan. 6-like reaction if Trump-supported candidates lose their elections during the midterms, Tillis was somber. 

"I think there's a risk. I really do," he said, adding, "It would be another unforced error if we do that."  

Tillis predicts Republicans are about to suffer an "electoral bloodbath" in the upcoming midterm elections, with bread-and-butter affordability issues a main concern. Still, he said many of his colleagues are afraid to break with the White House.

In his book, Tillis writes that at least 30 Republican senators have expressed reservations about many of Mr. Trump's actions, but usually are only willing to speak up privately, fearing that if the president decides to target them, their days will be numbered. 

"They don't want to bear the weight of the president. I get that. You're up for reelection? He'll target you in a primary. And so look, you know what all martyrs have in common? They're dead," Tillis said. "There were probably a few instances where if [you] kind of ripped the bandaid off early, then I think we'd have had a lot better midterm environment than we're confronted with now."

Read the full transcript of the segment.

This article originally appeared on CBS News at https://www.cbsnews.com/news/senator-thom-tillis-60-minutes/

item.title: FBI arrests suspected Chinese agent accused of surveilling Taiwan president's son
item.description:
The FBI arrested a suspected Chinese agent at Los Angeles International Airport after she allegedly surveilled the Taiwanese president's U.S.-based son, law enforcement sources told CBS News.

Wanying "Heather" Zhang, an Irvine, California, realtor, was cuffed by federal law enforcement on Sunday before she boarded a flight to Shanghai, China, from LAX, on a charge of acting as an unregistered agent of a foreign government.

Zhang's husband Edric Ding, a realtor at the same firm, told CBS News when reached by phone Sunday: "I don't know anything yet," and declined to comment further.

It was not immediately clear if Zhang has an attorney.

A criminal complaint, filed in federal court by a member of the FBI's counterintelligence squad in L.A., accused Zhang and an accomplice of traveling to Seattle, Washington, in September 2025 and taking pictures at the suburban home of a top Taiwanese official's family.

Law enforcement sources told CBS News that the target was Ting-Yu Lai, the son of Taiwanese President Ching-Te Lai.

Ting-Yu, an engineer in his 30s, attended college in America and has a young U.S.-born son with his wife, Hsiao Chen, according to Taiwanese media reports. He now works for the Dutch multinational electronics firm Philips.

"If the PRC [People's Republic of China] wish to obtain leverage over the President of Taiwan during any potential conflict, the location and pictures of the close relatives of a high-ranking Taiwanese government official, including pictures of their homes and cars, could be useful to the PRC," wrote FBI Special Agent Kevin Holt in the Oct. 3, 2026, criminal complaint.

Taiwan has been the focus of high geopolitical tensions for decades. It asserts its independence, while the Chinese government claims it is part of China. The island is in a key position astride major shipping lanes, and is where many of the world's most advanced semiconductor chips are manufactured.

CBS News reached out to the Taiwanese consulate for comment.

The complaint said Zhang, 34, and a man named only as "Individual 1" flew from Las Vegas to Seattle on Sept. 1, 2025, rented a black Nissan Rogue and drove to their target's home.

Images from a neighbor's security camera included in the complaint allegedly show the two "appearing to film" Ting-Yu, his wife and their child as they arrived home that evening.

CBS News matched the images to an address near Seattle owned by Ting-Yu.

Zhang allegedly texted her Chinese government handler: "Saw him. Young male. It's that young one," and "I am videorecording," followed by two license plate numbers, according to the complaint.

The FBI agent wrote that the texts from the Chinese messaging app WeChat were obtained from a search warrant on Zhang's iCloud account.

"Zhang was in contact with at least two people whom she appeared to acknowledge worked for the PRC government," the agent wrote.

The complaint claims  Zhang was introduced in June 2025 to one of the Chinese government officials by a classmate from her alma mater, Beijing's University of International Relations, which Holt said has close ties to the Ministry of State Security.

Holt's affidavit claims  Zhang booked a private room in Changsha, China, during a June 2025 trip, where she allegedly met the government official and received her surveillance mission.

She later texted the official, "I can take care of this thing," according to the complaint.

On Aug. 26, 2025, Zhang wrote: "I will be busy with work in L.A. this week. I will probably go to Seattle next week," and the official replied: "Ok. Thank you for your hard work," the complaint said.

Zhang is a licensed California realtor with JC Pacific Capital Inc. Her Zillow profile says she has 130 sales and listings around Los Angeles and neighboring counties. 

Ting-Yu received his bachelor's in electrical engineering from Case Western Reserve University in Cleveland, Ohio, in 2012; a master's in Bioengineering Innovation and Design from Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore, the following year; then a PhD from the Department of Bioengineering at the University of Washington, according to a profile from one of his academic publications.

Taiwan TV news station SETN reported that he met his Taiwanese wife while studying for his doctorate. They married in 2018 and had a child in the U.S. in 2020, according to CNA, Taiwan's national news agency.

Chinese government agents have previously been caught spying on and harassing Chinese dissidents and pro-democracy activists in the U.S.

Federal prosecutors said Shujun Wang, 75, infiltrated and informed on a Chinese pro-democracy group in Queens, New York, for the Chinese Ministry of State Security for 17 years. He was convicted in 2024 of acting as a foreign agent.

Two people were arrested in April 2023 for their involvement in an unofficial Chinese police station in Manhattan set up to monitor Chinese dissidents.

The Justice Department has warned of a plan by the Chinese security services called Operation Fox Hunt aimed at repatriating wanted Chinese nationals around the world, which targets enemies of the regime.

New York-based Quanzhong An, who prosecutors say is a leader of the U.S. wing of Operation Fox Hunt, was sentenced in March 2025 after harassing a Chinese dissident in an attempt to bring them back to China.

In California, former Arcadia Mayor Eileen Wang was charged with acting as a Chinese agent in May. She admitted to being paid to spread pro-Chinese government propaganda in the U.S., including an essay on her blog denying "forced labor" in China.

This article originally appeared on CBS News at https://www.cbsnews.com/news/chinese-agent-arrested-lax-taiwan-president-son/

item.title: FBI Director Kash Patel and country singer Alexis Wilkins announce they're engaged
item.description:
FBI Director Kash Patel is engaged to his country singer girlfriend, Alexis Wilkins, the pair announced in a post to X on Sunday evening.

Wilkins, 27, posted a black-and-white photo of herself standing with Patel, 46, flashing her hand in front of them to show off her ring with the caption, “Went and got the law involved.” The two have been dating since before Patel took over as head of the FBI in 2025, when she attended his swearing in.

The country singer and political commentator released her debut album in 2023. Wilkins has been affiliated with conservative groups and writes on her website that she “honors country tradition while adding relevance and current commentary.”

Patel, who reposted Wilkin's photo, has faced criticism for traveling on government aircraft on trips that have no known or apparent law enforcement purpose, including using an FBI jet to fly to State College, Pennsylvania, for a pro wrestling event where Wilkins performed the national anthem. Photos posted to social media by Wilkins afterward showed the couple smiling while she held an oversized golden championship belt.

Wilkins also made headlines as a performer at President Donald Trump's Great American State Fair on the National Mall as part of America 250, as other artists pulled out of the event after finding out it was not a non-partisan celebration.

This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/fbi-director-kash-patel-gets-005549284.html

item.title: 穷游火爆，青旅却彻底失宠了？
item.description:
2026-10-05 09:00:00

IC photo/ 图

近年来，曾经十分火爆的青旅倒了一片。据报道，目前中国（含香港）的认证青年旅舍数量仅109家，相比2017年的近300家，缩水了近三分之二。

在经济酒店降价、民宿崛起的背景下，青旅却在遇冷和倒闭。年轻人似乎不愿再为情怀买单，即便床位费便宜到几十块也难逃倒闭潮。

曾经火爆的青旅

其实“青年旅舍”这一概念的出现，已经是在一百多年前。1912年，世界上第一家青年旅舍在德国诞生，通过让住客共享宿舍和厨房设施，提供高性价比的住宿服务。随后，这个模式风靡全球。

随着“青年旅社”概念在全球的普及，1932年，欧洲诸国协会代表在阿姆斯特丹正式建立了国际青年旅社协会。到20世纪中后期，青旅成为全球性的社会文化现象。1988年，中国本土由广东省旅游局牵头，在广州及珠海等地建立了中国首批青年旅社，并逐渐风靡全国。后来，不仅知名旅游风景区有青旅，二、三线城市也多有之。

相对于酒店、宾馆这些住宿类型，青年旅社提供了按床位收费的多人间和公共空间（如大厅、厨房），价格则普遍比较低，很多青旅的费用在几十到一百多不等。并且因为有公共空间，也提供了一些社交可能。而宾馆、酒店则主打住宿。

对于青旅，或许一些中年人更为熟悉。39岁的梁月满十几年前在世界各地旅游时，住宿的首选都是青旅，甚至在旅途中认识了现在的丈夫。据她回忆，那时的青旅完全像一个由年轻人组成的“理想国”，来自五湖四海的人聚在一起，分享他们不同国籍、学历、职业的经历和故事，可以畅聊很久，甚至彻夜不眠。

网友阿杭则表示，十年前的青旅像是热闹的旅行情报交流站，是一个多元、互助且开放的公共空间，每晚大厅都坐满了玩音乐和侃大山的年轻人，大家聚在一起玩桌游、聊八卦、喝酒、讲故事。

可见，曾经的青旅正是以其开放性和包容性，吸引了不少的年轻人，也为他们提供了认识世界和现实社交的窗口。并且能让这些年轻人在意想不到之间，撞开新世界的大门。

青旅为何会衰落

那么，青旅为何会开始衰落呢？首先，是时代迎来了代际转换。青旅的核心竞争力曾是“廉价+社交”，但00后很多为“i人”，对共享空间、陌生社交的容忍度显著降低。

“敏感内耗的人住不了青旅的，”刘晨说，“自己睡不好，给别人添麻烦了也内耗心累。”尽管预算吃紧，最后她还是咬咬牙搬出了青旅，选择多掏100块，住进了附近的一家连锁快捷酒店。

广州一家青旅的店员陈霖告诉媒体，他工作的门店会在公共区域提供免费的咖啡，一楼就是一个巨大的自习室，大多数是长租客在使用。“刷招聘软件啊，或者准备考试的人比较多，旅游的住客一般都早出晚归的，就回来睡个觉，也不会在这里逗留很久。”

陈霖所在的青旅也曾要求店员邀请住客参与店里的活动，但回绝的住客往往占大多数。显然，青旅曾引以为傲的“公共性”，现在似乎正成了“社交压力放大器”。

同时，青旅的廉价优势也并不具有唯一性。酒店宾馆的降价促销，或者OTA平台给酒店宾馆发补贴，都能让价格便宜不少。并且，青旅的合居模式也存在卫生、财物等安全风险。对一些很重视卫生标准、人身安全等情况的人来说，青旅也非很好的选择。

虽然，目前穷游的理念依然在年轻人中盛行，但95后、00后的穷游理念是以最少的投入获得最大的体验，并不想牺牲旅游的质量。他们也相对注重隐私性。而由于线上社交的发达，社交似乎并不需要在线下旅社来达成。所以，在这种种因素的共同作用下，青旅就逐步在代际变换中走向衰落。

年轻人的新型住宿

随着时代的发展，年轻人在旅行住宿方面也开发了许多新模式。例如，自带帐篷睡袋，选择免费或低价露营地，既降低住宿成本又贴近自然，提升旅行的自由度。

另外，开着房车去旅行也成为不少年轻人的选择。此前，37名由90后及00后组成的年轻人就从广州出发，开着房车前往汕尾，体验了一把两天一晚的房车露营之旅。这种下车可以露营、烧烤、开派对，上车能洗澡、睡觉、唱K的旅居模式也带来了全新的体验。

除此之外，在洗浴中心过夜也成了一种选择。“出去旅游，只要花两百多块钱，一天的吃、住、休闲项目全有了。”市民郭小姐说，这次去东北旅游第一站的住宿地是洗浴中心。“洗浴中心提供一天四餐和全时段水果饮料，还有游戏室、棋牌室、KTV，当然还有洗浴和温泉。虽然住宿有点吵，但是价格在这摆着呢，太划算了。”

交换房屋，也成了一些网友的选择。早前，一位家住哈尔滨冰雪大世界旁的网友，就与福建湄洲岛的网友达成了换房协议，开启了一场别开生面的换房旅行。这种你住我家、我住你家的方式，也为一些网友带来了需要的便利。

近来，还有网友选择拼楼酒店的模式来住宿。以杭州的一栋高层大楼为例，整栋楼内分布着十余家酒店，几乎实现了每层一家的密集布局。

00后大学生叶雨欣在毕业旅行时直言：“不是酒店开不起，而是拼楼更有性价比。以前换酒店要拖着行李满街跑，现在整栋楼都是后备选择库，不满意随时换，还能体验不同风格。”

背包客陈群称之为“垂直社交城堡”：在A酒店大堂喝咖啡，去B酒店餐厅用餐，约朋友到C酒店空中酒吧赏夜景，一次入住即可解锁多个公共空间。

未来，随着年轻人代际的更迭和需求变化，也将为旅游住宿行业注入新的活力。行业在场景化体验、智能便捷和空间效率等方面，都有继续拓展的可能。更多元化的形态出现，也会推动行业在差异互补中继续发展。
